frameworks, standards, and governance that keep the brand coherent as the portfolio and products evolve. partner with creative, content, and customer marketing teams so the brand is expressed detail.desc: company description:rafiki coalition for health and wellness is a san francisco-based nonprofit dedicated to eliminating health inequities and improving the lives of black, african american, and marginalized communities in the bay area. for over 35 years, we have provided a safe, welcoming space where health, healing, and hope come together. we offer a holistic range of services, including free and low-cost health screenings, hiv prevention and care, mental health counseling, housing and economic support, fitness classes, and nutrition programs. guided by a belief that wellness is more than the absence of illness, we embrace a whole-person approach that honors the cultural, social, and emotional needs of our community.at rafiki, we are more than a service provider. we are a trusted partner, advocate, and resource. our work is rooted in compassion, cultural humility, and a commitment to social justice. every day, our team stands with our community to dismantle barriers, amplify voices, and create pathways to health and opportunity.if you're looking to join a mission-driven organization where your work directly empowers individuals and strengthens communities, rafiki coalition is the place to make a meaningful impactjob description:under the direction of the director of development and communications, the communications manager leads rafiki coalition's internal and external communications. the position develops clear, consistent messaging; manages digital and print communications; supports media and community outreach; and increases awareness of rafiki's mission, programs, services, and impact. the communications manager also supports development activities through fundraising communications, donor materials, sponsorship promotion, and funder-facing content. the position may supervise staff, contractors, interns, or volunteers assigned to communications projects. responsibilities communications strategy and brand management develop and implement annual communications and marketing plans aligned with organizational priorities and approved by the executive director. maintain consistent messaging, voice, visual identity, and use of the rafiki coalition brand across departments, programs, campaigns, and public materials. create communications calendars, establish priorities and deadlines, and coordinate information from staff and program leaders. monitor communications results and provide practical reports and recommendations to the executive director. content and publications write, edit, and coordinate print and electronic materials, including newsletters, brochures, fact sheets, presentations, flyers, organizational updates, and the annual report. translate program information, community needs, and organizational results into accurate, accessible, and culturally responsive content for varied audiences. manage the review and approval process for public-facing materials and maintain organized communications files, templates, photographs, and content resources. coordinate designers, printers, photographers, videographers, and other vendors as needed. digital communications manage website content and coordinate website maintenance to keep information accurate, current, accessible, and easy to use. plan, create, schedule, and monitor social media and email communications in support of programs, events, community education, and organizational priorities. maintain digital content standards and use basic analytics to assess reach, engagement, and opportunities for improvement. coordinate timely communications during urgent, sensitive, or rapidly changing situations, in consultation with the executive director and appropriate leaders. media community and partner relations develop media outreach materials, including press releases, media advisories, background information, talking points, opinion pieces, and responses to media inquiries. build and maintain working relationships with media, community partners, coalitions, issue experts, and organizations serving rafiki's communities. support public events, campaigns, and community engagement activities through messaging, promotion, materials, and communications logistics. prepare the executive director and other designated representatives for interviews, presentations, public statements, and community appearances. development support partner with the executive director, development staff, and consultants to create fundraising appeals, donor communications, sponsorship materials, campaign content, and event promotion. contribute communications content for grant proposals, funder reports, acknowledgments, impact stories, and other development materials. help communicate the results of funded programs accurately and consistently while meeting applicable funder recognition requirements. support donor and sponsor cultivation through coordinated messaging and appropriate communications follow-up. planning administration and supervision develop and monitor the communications budget; manage vendors, contracts, schedules, and project deliverables within approved authority. coordinate multiple projects, clarify roles and approvals, and keep the executive director informed of progress, risks, deadlines, and decisions needed. supervise and train assigned staff, contractors, interns, or volunteers and provide clear expectations and feedback. follow organizational policies and protect confidential, sensitive, and personally identifiable information in all communications. perform other duties as assigned.requirements:bachelor's degree in communications, marketing, journalism, public relations, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience. at least five years of progressively responsible experience in communications, marketing, public relations, or related work, preferably in a nonprofit or community-based organization. strong writing, editing, verbal communication, interpersonal, and project management skills, with careful attention to accuracy and detail. experience managing websites, email communications, social media, publications, media relations, and communications vendors or consultants. ability to communicate effectively with diverse communities and represent rafiki's mission and work in a culturally responsive manner. working knowledge of microsoft office and common content management, email marketing, social media, design, and analytics tools. additional information:this is a full time positionhybrid flsa status - exempt application instructions:when applying for the position include with your resume a cover letter explaining:why you are a strong candidate for this positionwhy you are interested in working for rafiki compensation details: 88000-95000 yearly salary

content is highly engaging, discoverable, and optimized for the consumer and patient journeys across applications and platforms and seamlessly integrated into the clinical workflow. your goal is to help simplify complex strategic ideas and transform them into actionable, accessible education that empowers consumers to manage their health, while collaborating on ai-enabled content orchestration and governance, ensuring our content is optimized for the latest generative and agentic technologies.editorial strategyeditorial mission: to provide consumers with the most trusted, accessible, and dynamic assets that surface at the right moment of care in the right format.process designcontent lifecycle: you will collaborate on the lifecycle of high-volume assets, from research and intake to for emr data exchange.ai content recommendations: work with technical teams on ai-driven clinical decision support that merges encounter data with ambient ai transcripts to improve real-time content recommendations for clinicians.content design: work with the knowledge engineering and search teams to identify "intent gaps" in our consumer and patient libraries and develop content that answers the questions people are actually asking online, as well as what our clients and their patients need.workflow & operationsai enablement & product integration: lead training and enablement for team members and freelancers to incorporate ai agents and automations into every aspect of content strategy and development. partner with product and tech on uat and training for ai-driven products.intake & prioritization: manage the "front door" for new content and asset requests, using data to prioritize high-impact consumer health and patient education projects over other projects.process improvement: continuously partner on refining the content and asset production workflows to reduce "time-to-market" and "time-to-delivery" through ai-assisted automation of clinical and content detail.desc: maintainx is a leading mobile-first work execution platform for industrial and frontline teams. more than 13,000 customers, including duracell, mcdonald's, shell, dhl and volvo, use maintainx to cut unplanned downtime and run better operations, across 13.9 million managed assets and 79.5 million completed work orders.in august 2026 maintainx became part of autodesk, joining autodesk operations solutions, the organization unifying autodesk's operations platform alongside tandem, flexsim and fusion operations. autodesk's strategy is to converge design, make and operate into one continuous lifecycle: design an asset, build it, run it, then feed what you learn running it back into the next design. autodesk had design and make. operate is the phase that tells you what actually happened, and it is ours.role contextthis role sits on the brand design team inside marketing, the brand and motion designers behind our campaigns, web, launches and events. every piece of that work moves through asana, and this person owns how it comes in, how it moves and how it ships. you'll be the reason designers spend their days designing.the roleyou will own the operating rhythm of the brand design team, from the moment a request lands to the moment the work ships.own intake in asana. review new requests with marketing stakeholders, make sure each arrives with a complete creative brief, and prioritize what the team takes on, cutting the back-and-forth that pulls designers away from design.build and maintain the processes that move work smoothly from request to delivery, consistently adapting and optimizing.partner with marketing program management on large marketing initiatives each year that touch every marketer, setting start dates and deliverable milestones with clear reasoning behind them.track team capacity against demand and raise trade-offs early, so deadlines are decisions rather than surprises.keep project files and deliverables organized so anything the team has made can be found in seconds.build the reporting that shows what the team delivers and the impact of that work, in both qualitative and quantitative terms.you'll report to our director of marketing creative, and work alongside a team of designers and motion designers.about youyou've run project delivery for an in-house creative, design or marketing team.you've owned intake and set the standard for a good brief, and you've gotten requesters to follow it.you're fluent in a work management tool. asana is ours.you plan across many teams, set milestones, and turn scattered feedback into clear next steps.you notice what's broken before anyone tells you and arrive with a proposed fix.you influence through rationale, data and diplomacy, and you're clearly on your stakeholders' team. people want to work with you because you serve the company as a whole rather than defending any one group.nice to haveexperience reporting on the outcomes of creative work with datafamiliarity with brand or motion design workflowsbackground in b2b software or industrial marketingwe offerwork that shows up in the physical world. the brand you help ship supports software that keeps factories, fleets, hospitals and campuses running.a product the industry already loves. you're adding to something that already wins, and the work is about what comes next.autodesk scale, same mission. the resources of a profitable public company, pointed at the problem we were already solving: building the operating layer between how the physical world is designed and how it performs.an early seat. how this team operates is being shaped right now, and you'll be able to name the parts you own.values & how we workwe reward output and trust people with autonomy. you'll have real room to redesign how this team works, and we expect you to use it: raise issues early, bring a proposed fix, and measure whether it worked. we hire for what you've done, not what your title was. show us the project you're proudest of.our mission is to keep the physical world running. factories, fleets, hospitals and campuses stay up because the people who maintain them have tools worth using. 4482197240.title: Sr. Manager, Future of Work Communications, Global Operations and Workplace Reputation

detail.desc: descriptionai, automation, and robotics are transforming how the world works, and amazon, as one of the largest employers on the planet, has a unique opportunity to lead the way in preparing people for what comes next. this role puts you at the center of that effort, at an unprecedented technological moment, shaping programs and communications that will touch tens of millions of lives.as sr pr manager, future of work communications, you will define, build, own, and maintain the future ready campaign: a cross-channel effort anchored by amazon's $2.5 billion commitment to help 50 million people grow their skills for in-demand jobs by 2030 and built on the company's successful track record of upskilling. you won't just tell the story; you'll help shape the programs behind it. that means building, scaling, and maintaining campaigns end-to-end, from the ground up: identifying the opportunity, sourcing data to inform your approach, developing programs that address it, and working with teams across the company to bring them to life through earned, owned, and social media, third-party voices, and strategic partnerships.you're a big thinker and a storyteller at your core. you thrive in ambiguity, can start from a future vision (maybe years down the road) and work backwards to understand how we get there, and you think both globally and locally. you generate ideas relentlessly, and when one doesn't land, you learn from it and come back with something better. you look around corners, anticipating what could become an issue, where a story could go, and which stakeholders need to be brought in early so the team can stay ahead of the moment. you aren't afraid to push back, challenge assumptions, hold partners accountable, even at senior levels, or debate strategies with leaders at every level, because you know that's how good work becomes great. you navigate complex stakeholder dynamics across business, legal, policy, and communications teams, aligning on positioning, timing, and sequencing for announcements that carry significant external visibility.you use your storytelling skill to get ahead of challenges, not just react to them. you'll stay close to how conversations around ai, innovation, and the future of work are evolving, helping the business understand emerging trends and shape thoughtful, proactive communications. you’ll help position amazon’s investments and innovation in a way that resonates with employees, customers, and external audiences. when issues arise, you’ll bring sound judgment and a thoughtful communications approach to help the team navigate them effectively.this is a strong independent contributor role that will have access to additional support from members of the broader team as needed but isn't responsible for direct management. it reports into the global operations and workplace reputation communications team within global corporate communications.key job responsibilitiesdevelop and execute complex communications programs that require input from internal and external leaders, defining strategy where none currently exists and ensuring alignment with organizational objectives.build and maintain cooperative relationships with media outlet representatives, engaging regularly to secure impactful coverage and manage reputational narratives.partner with cross-functional stakeholders to prioritize communications initiatives, making smart trade-offs on timing, effort, and deliverables while establishing clear and measurable success criteria.identify and assess reputational and sentiment risks, establishing protocols and engaging the right partners to take timely, appropriate action.author and review high-quality written materials—including narratives, communications plans, and business documents—providing guidance on writing excellence and ensuring alignment with team and organizational goals.a day in the lifeyou might start your morning reviewing media coverage and sentiment data to brief a leader ahead of an important announcement. by midday, you could be working with a cross-functional team to brainstorm new global program offerings for the workforce of tomorrow, pressure-testing assumptions and aligning stakeholders on messaging. in the afternoon, you may connect with media contacts to pitch a story or hear what trends they're most interested in, then close out by reviewing metrics and updating your team's communications roadmap to keep programs on track.about the teamwe're a team of strategic communicators who are responsible for amplifying and protecting amazon's reputation as a good employer and an innovator that's shaping the workplace of tomorrow for our teams and the world around us. we work across organizational boundaries to develop durable communications strategies that inform, engage, and build trust with the audiences that matter most. we use data to shape our decisions, and we anticipate and mitigate reputational headwinds through cross-channel efforts. we value thoughtful collaboration, creative problem-solving, and a commitment to getting the details right.we're building for the long term—investing in mechanisms, relationships, and talent that will scale as amazon grows. if you want to do meaningful work alongside colleagues who care deeply about their craft and support each other's growth, this is the team for you.basic qualifications 10+ years of recent professional communications or public relations experience bachelor's degree experience driving direction and alignment with cross-functional teams proven track record of building and scaling integrated, multi-channel campaigns with measurable results across earned, owned, and paid media strong storytelling instincts and creative ideation skills, with a track record of generating ambitious, high-impact campaign concepts and translating complex policy topics into compelling narratives experience diving deep on unfamiliar topics and using data to develop messaging frameworks and net-new narratives that influence various audiencespreferred qualifications experience communicating complex concepts clearly and persuasively to different audiences experience working in a fast-paced and ambiguous environment, or experience delivering results for large, cross-functional initiatives/projects experience earning buy-in, influencing decisions, offering different perspectives, and communicating results to senior leadership experience using data to define ambiguous reputational opportunities and develop durable solutions, going beyond communications to shape the programs themselves experience identifying emerging trends and informing business leadership of evolving reputational headwinds and opportunitiesamazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.our inclusive culture empowers amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. if you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. if the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your recruiting partner.the base salary range for this position is listed below. your amazon package will include sign-on payments and restricted stock units (rsus). final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. amazon also offers comprehensive benefits including health insurance (medical, dental, vision, prescription, basic life & ad&d insurance and option for supplemental life plans, eap, mental health support, medical advice line, flexible spending accounts, adoption and surrogacy reimbursement coverage), 401(k) matching, paid time off, and parental leave. learn more about our benefits at https://amazon.jobs/en/benefits.usa, ny, new york - 191,000.00 - 257,800.00 usd annuallyusa, tn, nashville - 156,200.00 - 211,000.00 usd annuallyusa, va, arlington - 173,600.00 - 234,400.00 usd annuallyusa, wa, seattle - 173,600.00 - 234,400.00 usd annuallycompany - amazon.com services llcjob id: a10583322

about hiyaat hiya, we’re making business calls more trusted, useful, and effective.voice remains one of the most important ways businesses communicate with their customers, but the value of a call depends on trust. when customers do not recognize who is calling or why, important conversations are missed, customer relationships suffer, and business outcomes are harder to achieve.hiya helps businesses create trusted calling experiences that benefit both sides of the conversation: enterprises can reach customers with confidence, and customers can answer with confidence. our products support branded business calling, trusted caller identity, call performance insights, customer engagement, and voice security capabilities that help businesses strengthen relationships and improve outcomes.this role sits in a core business area for hiya and is focused on helping smb and enterprise customers succeed.about the rolethis year we rewrote our story from the ground up — who we are, why we matter, and where we're going. now we need someone to take that story global and make hiya the voice the world trusts on the future of the phone call.this is the role where it all comes together. you'll own how the world sees hiya: the press, the analysts, the stages, our social channels, and the creative that ties it into one unmistakable brand. and it's a story with real range. the same hiya has to land with a network executive in madrid deciding how to protect millions of subscribers from ai scams, a sales leader in toronto whose team's calls keep going unanswered, and a mom in ohio who just got a deepfake call pretending to be her son asking for money.you'll lead our existing creative + events teams and pr agencies, you'll build, and you'll get your hands dirty. organic social doesn't exist here yet. you'll write the strategy, find our voice, and ship the first posts yourself. this is a director role for someone who still loves doing the work.what you'll doown the brand. take the new narrative from slides to everywhere hiya shows up, and set the visual and verbal identity so every touchpoint looks and sounds like one hiya. give teams what they need to stay on brand without asking permission.flex the story without breaking it. work with product marketing to tell it right for each audience, then make it land in each country, with its own pains and language.set global pr strategy. decide where we invest market by market, including how pr helps us break into new ones. lead our agencies and keep the narrative owned in-house.turn our data into headlines. make our annual state of the call report the one reporters, analysts, and operators wait for, and keep a steady drumbeat of data stories by market.build analyst relations. get hiya in front of the analysts who shape how operators and businesses buy, and make sure they know our story cold.build organic social as a function, not just a channel. grow our executives' voices, set guardrails with legal so the team can move fast, create ideas that travel across paid, owned, earned, and ai search, and turn what we hear into intel for product, sales, and pr.make hiya a visible industry leader. build the thought leadership and speaking program, prep spokespeople, and go after the keynotes and awards that put us at the center of voice security and ai fraud. have a plan ready for when something goes sideways.make events count. with our global events manager, set the event strategy: which events matter for which audiences, how we show up, and how we measure presence and relationships, not just leads. flagship moments like mobile world congress should feel unmistakably hiya.build and lead the team. coach and grow the team, run our agencies, and build a creative function that scales globally. hire for where we're going.measure what matters: share of voice, coverage quality, analyst perception, and how brand, pr, and social move people from awareness to consideration. use it to decide where to invest.what we are looking foryou've led brand and comms before. you have 10+ years in brand, communications, or pr at b2b tech companies, including leading teams and agencies across multiple countries.a leader who still does the work. you set the strategy, then write the pitch, draft the post, and give the designer specific feedback yourself. you're as comfortable managing as you are doing.a team builder. you've grown creative or comms teams from small to scaled.a storyteller with taste. you can make telecom, ai, and fraud interesting enough that a reporter leans in, and you know great creative when you see it. b2b buzzwords make you wince.consistent without being rigid. you've kept a brand coherent across audiences, products, and countries, and you know when to flex and when to hold the line.strong across pr, analyst relations, and social. these are your core skills, not side projects. you have real media and analyst relationships, ideally in tech, telecom, or security, and you've turned social from a posting calendar into a real function.global by default. you've run comms across the us and europe, and you know a story that works in new york can fall flat in madrid.calm in a storm. you've handled issues and crisis comms and know how to protect trust when it counts.hands-on and experimental with ai. our pms are already vibe-coding fixes to production. you'll use ai daily to move faster and keep the quality bar high.comfortable on stage and in the room with executives, operators, and press.how we workhiya is not a passive environment. we expect people to take ownership, form opinions, and engage directly with hard problems.we work with a high degree of transparency and autonomy. context is shared openly, and decisions are discussed, challenged, and then made. once a call is made, we commit and move forward.you'll be expected to work through ambiguity, weigh tradeoffs, and take responsibility for results, while keeping a high bar for quality and customer trust.every team member at hiya is expected to live our core values:serve, our customers and partners by holding a high bar for trust and qualityown, share in success and open up to failureslead, listen, show up with a point of view but commit entirely once a decision has been madeimprove, even if it means changing course or contradicting ourselvesdo, rather than observehow we invest in youcompensation & ownershipequity compensation: ownership aligned with your impact and the company's growthwe offer an l&d budget to support your growth and real internal mobility so career pathing isn't just a talking point — because we're building this with people who own the outcome.come work with us!we're building a team with diverse perspectives, identities, and professional experiences. we evaluate candidates through a business lens and believe that diversity and unique viewpoints make our company stronger, more dynamic, and a great place to build a career.we've been recognized by built in, geekwire, comparably, g2, forbes, and deloitte technology fast 500 for our culture, innovation, leadership, compensation, and more. at hiya, we're a people-centric company focused on helping each employee grow both personally and professionally. we create a culture of support and empowerment that challenges the status quo, resulting in an energized team that's passionate about their work. you'll love working here if you're looking for an innovative challenge that's disrupting an industry. come join us!hiya is an equal opportunity employer. we celebrate diversity and are committed to building an inclusive environment for all employees.

from the professional educator standards board. this position, located in olympia, wa, may be eligible for a partial teleworking schedule. telework combines in-building and off-site days.who we arewe believe that the success of washington’s students depends on the success of washington’s educators. at the professional educator standards board (pesb), we strengthen and support the success of our educator workforce through every stage of their career.we are one agency with two governing boards: the professional educator standards board and the paraeducator board. our policies and programs span washington’s system of educator pathways, preparation, certification, and professional development opportunities. we oversee educator standards and licensure, and hold preparation programs accountable for the ways in which they recruit, support, and prepare diverse and classroom-ready educators.our board members and staff are committed to centering diversity, equity, and inclusion in every aspect of our work and to building respectful, reciprocal relationships with tribal nations across washington state. as part of our commitment, we embrace the opportunity to address disparities and barriers perpetuated by historical and institutionalized racism within the overall education system, and we recognize the unique government-to-government relationship the state holds with tribal nations under the centennial accord.our agency values serve as a compass to guide our work. we value:educator voicediversity, equity, and inclusioneducator excellence for student successcommunity engagementlearning and innovationto operate as an antiracist agency, we seek candidates aligned with these values, including candidates who bring experience or a genuine willingness to learn how to work in good faith with education partners, diverse constituencies, and tribal nations. passion for the mission of pesb, including its commitment to equity and to honoring washington’s diverse communities and tribal nations.position overviewthis position provides strategic guidance to the executive director and other agency members to help engage the public, strengthen external partnerships, and promote the value and visibility of our work. the director for communication and external relations must establish strong, collaborative relationships with internal teams to execute effective, equity-centered communications plans supporting agency needs and goals.this role ensures communication with educators, paraeducators, preparation programs, school districts, educational service districts (esds), educational organizations, policymakers, the public, and tribal nations in washington state is not only clear and accurate but also culturally responsive, reflecting the histories, sovereignty, and self-determination of the communities we serve. the director partners closely with the agency’s tribal liaison to ensure tribal perspectives, protocols, and priorities are embedded in the agency’s communications, outreach, and public engagement work.the director will employ equity-centered and culturally responsive communications to elevate the agency’s core functions for educators (career exploration and discovery, preparation, credentialing, workforce development, and shortage). the role will also work to ensure the agency’s messaging reflects the needs of historically underserved communities and tribal nations. this role will lead and support the development and implementation of campaigns for multiple audiences to support the agency’s priorities, including legislative advocacy.key responsibilitiesagencywide communicationswrite, edit, and design agency communications materials, including one-pagers, reports, faqs, and presentations, to effectively communicate information to diverse audiences (e.g., educators, legislators, stakeholders, associations, tribal nations, and community members). ensure materials are accurate, accessible, culturally responsive, aligned with key messages, and promote the agency as a positive and transparent policymaker and partner.create and maintain internal policies, processes, and training to guide and support staff on the use of communications tools, including guidance on culturally responsive communications practices.promote agencywide initiatives and programs by developing key messages and talking points, leading audience analysis activities, implementing communications plans, and assessing opportunities for greater engagement and outreach. provide media and outreach guidance for agency meetings and conferences, develop materials, and recommend promotional strategies to increase visibility, registration, and participation from diverse audiences and tribal communities.alongside the legislative policy team, translate complex policy, rulemaking, and certification/credentialing information into accessible language for diverse audiences.align current and new agency materials with ada requirements and accessibility best practices.support agency tribal liaison in maintaining relationships between the board and tribal education departments, tribal colleges, and tribal leadership on matters related to educator standards and requirements, the john mccoy (lulilaš) since time immemorial curriculum, tribal-based teacher and paraeducator pathways, and workforce development.public relations and legislative supportdevelop and implement campaigns for multiple audiences to support legislative advocacy for agency initiatives.work closely with the executive director and staff to support the agency’s legislative priorities by advising on communications strategy, framing, positioning, and research, ensuring an equity and tribal relations lens is applied throughout. cultivate and maintain knowledge of and relationships with educational organizations, policymakers, tribal nations, and other partners and constituencies as needed.ensure consistent messaging in legislative materials such as fact sheets, talking points, and presentations.track media coverage, write press releases, coordinate interviews, identify story opportunities, and maintain consistent and positive press relationships. serve as the first point of contact and agency spokesperson for media inquiries.provide direct and proactive advice, consultation, and assistance to the executive director and staff, as needed, regarding public information matters, including providing direct assistance in researching, providing information, and developing messages. support the tribal liaison with establishing, cultivating, and maintaining government-to-government relationships with washington’s tribal nations, consistent with the state’s centennial accord and related tribal consultation policies.digital communicationsmanage graphic design for agency materials, including one-pagers, reports, faqs, ada compliance, and presentations to effectively communicate information to diverse audiences (e.g., educators, legislators, stakeholders, associations, and community members). manage the design and execution of social media, collaborating with agency teams to identify social media content, using best practices, engagement tactics, user-experience design strategies, accessibility compliance, and strengthening content through plain talk principles that reach diverse audiences.manage agency social media tools and profiles, including the content calendar, facebook, x (formerly known as twitter), linkedin, medium, and youtube. lead the design, management, and detail.desc: descriptionai, automation, and robotics are transforming how the world works, and amazon, as one of the largest employers on the planet, has a unique opportunity to lead the way in preparing people for what comes next. this role puts you at the center of that effort, at an unprecedented technological moment, shaping programs and communications that will touch tens of millions of lives.as sr pr manager, future of work communications, you will define, build, own, and maintain the future ready campaign: a cross-channel effort anchored by amazon's $2.5 billion commitment to help 50 million people grow their skills for in-demand jobs by 2030 and built on the company's successful track record of upskilling. you won't just tell the story; you'll help shape the programs behind it. that means building, scaling, and maintaining campaigns end-to-end, from the ground up: identifying the opportunity, sourcing data to inform your approach, developing programs that address it, and working with teams across the company to bring them to life through earned, owned, and social media, third-party voices, and strategic partnerships.you're a big thinker and a storyteller at your core. you thrive in ambiguity, can start from a future vision (maybe years down the road) and work backwards to understand how we get there, and you think both globally and locally. you generate ideas relentlessly, and when one doesn't land, you learn from it and come back with something better. you look around corners, anticipating what could become an issue, where a story could go, and which stakeholders need to be brought in early so the team can stay ahead of the moment. you aren't afraid to push back, challenge assumptions, hold partners accountable, even at senior levels, or debate strategies with leaders at every level, because you know that's how good work becomes great. you navigate complex stakeholder dynamics across business, legal, policy, and communications teams, aligning on positioning, timing, and sequencing for announcements that carry significant external visibility.you use your storytelling skill to get ahead of challenges, not just react to them. you'll stay close to how conversations around ai, innovation, and the future of work are evolving, helping the business understand emerging trends and shape thoughtful, proactive communications. you’ll help position amazon’s investments and innovation in a way that resonates with employees, customers, and external audiences. when issues arise, you’ll bring sound judgment and a thoughtful communications approach to help the team navigate them effectively.this is a strong independent contributor role that will have access to additional support from members of the broader team as needed but isn't responsible for direct management. it reports into the global operations and workplace reputation communications team within global corporate communications.key job responsibilitiesdevelop and execute complex communications programs that require input from internal and external leaders, defining strategy where none currently exists and ensuring alignment with organizational objectives.build and maintain cooperative relationships with media outlet representatives, engaging regularly to secure impactful coverage and manage reputational narratives.partner with cross-functional stakeholders to prioritize communications initiatives, making smart trade-offs on timing, effort, and deliverables while establishing clear and measurable success criteria.identify and assess reputational and sentiment risks, establishing protocols and engaging the right partners to take timely, appropriate action.author and review high-quality written materials—including narratives, communications plans, and business documents—providing guidance on writing excellence and ensuring alignment with team and organizational goals.a day in the lifeyou might start your morning reviewing media coverage and sentiment data to brief a leader ahead of an important announcement. by midday, you could be working with a cross-functional team to brainstorm new global program offerings for the workforce of tomorrow, pressure-testing assumptions and aligning stakeholders on messaging. in the afternoon, you may connect with media contacts to pitch a story or hear what trends they're most interested in, then close out by reviewing metrics and updating your team's communications roadmap to keep programs on track.about the teamwe're a team of strategic communicators who are responsible for amplifying and protecting amazon's reputation as a good employer and an innovator that's shaping the workplace of tomorrow for our teams and the world around us. we work across organizational boundaries to develop durable communications strategies that inform, engage, and build trust with the audiences that matter most. we use data to shape our decisions, and we anticipate and mitigate reputational headwinds through cross-channel efforts. we value thoughtful collaboration, creative problem-solving, and a commitment to getting the details right.we're building for the long term—investing in mechanisms, relationships, and talent that will scale as amazon grows. if you want to do meaningful work alongside colleagues who care deeply about their craft and support each other's growth, this is the team for you.basic qualifications 10+ years of recent professional communications or public relations experience bachelor's degree experience driving direction and alignment with cross-functional teams proven track record of building and scaling integrated, multi-channel campaigns with measurable results across earned, owned, and paid media strong storytelling instincts and creative ideation skills, with a track record of generating ambitious, high-impact campaign concepts and translating complex policy topics into compelling narratives experience diving deep on unfamiliar topics and using data to develop messaging frameworks and net-new narratives that influence various audiencespreferred qualifications experience communicating complex concepts clearly and persuasively to different audiences experience working in a fast-paced and ambiguous environment, or experience delivering results for large, cross-functional initiatives/projects experience earning buy-in, influencing decisions, offering different perspectives, and communicating results to senior leadership experience using data to define ambiguous reputational opportunities and develop durable solutions, going beyond communications to shape the programs themselves experience identifying emerging trends and informing business leadership of evolving reputational headwinds and opportunitiesamazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.our inclusive culture empowers amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. if you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. if the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your recruiting partner.the base salary range for this position is listed below. your amazon package will include sign-on payments and restricted stock units (rsus). final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. amazon also offers comprehensive benefits including health insurance (medical, dental, vision, prescription, basic life & ad&d insurance and option for supplemental life plans, eap, mental health support, medical advice line, flexible spending accounts, adoption and surrogacy reimbursement coverage), 401(k) matching, paid time off, and parental leave. learn more about our benefits at https://amazon.jobs/en/benefits.usa, ny, new york - 191,000.00 - 257,800.00 usd annuallyusa, tn, nashville - 156,200.00 - 211,000.00 usd detail.desc: role overviewas a content strategist at webmd ignite, you will guide the strategic vision for our patient education assets in support of multiple products and solutions. you will ensure that our content is highly engaging, discoverable, and optimized for the consumer and patient journeys across applications and platforms and seamlessly integrated into the clinical workflow. your goal is to help simplify complex strategic ideas and transform them into actionable, accessible education that empowers consumers to manage their health, while collaborating on ai-enabled content orchestration and governance, ensuring our content is optimized for the latest generative and agentic technologies.editorial strategyeditorial mission: to provide consumers with the most trusted, accessible, and actionable health education that drives better health decisions and patient engagement, and empowers providers and patients with timely, evidence-based education that improves clinical workflow.target audience: consumers, patients, and family caregivers seeking health information across various digital touchpoints, as well as clinicians, health system administrators, and care managers.point of view: we advocate for the user. we believe health education should be clear, jargon-free, and designed for health literacy—meeting the user where they are in their care journey. our content is "fhir-friendly," interoperable, and "ai-ready," designed as modular assets for dynamic assembly by conversational and agentic systems. we believe health education should not be a static document but dynamic assets that surface at the right moment of care in the right format.process designcontent lifecycle: you will collaborate on the lifecycle of high-volume assets, from research and intake to production. you will also collaborate on ai-assisted workflows, including metadata management and summarization in the content management system to continually increase the ratio of work automated with ai.success metrics: measure strategy effectiveness through feedback on content findability, gaps, gluts, and change requests. success will also be measured by gains in efficiency and scale driven by ai-enabled orchestration.key responsibilitiessubstance & editorial directionstrategic roadmapping: define the content themes and project priorities that align with consumer health trends, clinical health trends, and client needs for consumer engagement and patient education.ai & clinical auditing: utilize agentic ai for automated governance, auditing activities, and programmatic asset mapping for both internal and external use cases. leverage ai for automated clinical auditing and "drift" detection to ensure content aligns with evolving medical guidelines, automatically flagging outdated items for review.market alignment: engage with clients and prospects to understand their jobs to be done, translating them into editorial solutions to support “self-serve” use cases and emr integrations.product collaboration: partner with ux and product managers to ensure content is "born digital"—designed to work seamlessly within modern application layouts, mobile interfaces, and clinical workflows.interoperability & discoverabilityfhir support: partner with content integration and knowledge engineering to align content and metadata models, ensuring our library is "fhir-ready" for emr data exchange.ai content recommendations: work with technical teams on ai-driven clinical decision support that merges encounter data with ambient ai transcripts to improve real-time content recommendations for clinicians.content design: work with the knowledge engineering and search teams to identify "intent gaps" in our consumer and patient libraries and develop content that answers the questions people are actually asking online, as well as what our clients and their patients need.workflow & operationsai enablement & product integration: lead training and enablement for team members and freelancers to incorporate ai agents and automations into every aspect of content strategy and development. partner with product and tech on uat and training for ai-driven products.intake & prioritization: manage the "front door" for new content and asset requests, using data to prioritize high-impact consumer health and patient education projects over other projects.process improvement: continuously partner on refining the content and asset production workflows to reduce "time-to-market" and "time-to-delivery" through ai-assisted automation of clinical and content tasks.qualificationsprofessional experienceeducation: bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, public health, health education, or a related field (master’s level preferred).experience: 5+ years in content strategy or patient education, specifically focused on b2c (business-to-consumer) health or wellness products, or with a proven track record in the healthcare or healthit sectors.digital health ecosystems: familiar with patient education content strategy principles, with the ability to align assets effectively for consumers, providers, payers, and health it users.technical skillsai proficiency: understands ai methodologies, including prompt engineering, rag-optimized response systems, and working with agentic ai autonomous operational partners.cms, workflow, and crm tools: proficiency in using a variety of content management, project management, and client management tools.analytics: ability to interpret client, clinical, and consumer behavior data using a variety of analytic tools and outputs.core competenciesuser-centricity & ai orchestration: a passion for improving user journeys with content, harness is the ai software delivery platform company, led by technologist and entrepreneur jyoti bansal (founder of appdynamics, acquired by cisco for $3.7b). harness has raised approximately $570m in funding and is valued at $5.5b, backed by leading investors including goldman sachs, menlo ventures, ivp, unusual ventures, citi ventures, and more. as ai accelerates code creation, the real bottleneck has shifted to everything after the code – testing, deployments, application security, reliability, compliance, and cost optimization. harness brings ai and automation to this “outer loop,” helping teams ship software faster while maintaining security and governance throughout the entire software delivery lifecycle.powered by harness ai and the software delivery knowledge graph, the harness platform applies deep context and intelligent automation across the software delivery lifecycle with governance and policy-driven controls embedded throughout the platform.over the past year, harness powered over 185m deployments, 82m builds, 18t flag evaluations, 8m security scans, 9.1b optimized tests, 3t protected api calls, and helped manage $2.8b in cloud spend — enabling customers like united airlines, morningstar, and choice hotels to accelerate releases by up to 75%, reduce cloud costs by up to 60%, and achieve 10x devops efficiency.with a global team across 26 offices and 27 countries, harness is shaping the future of ai software delivery — and we’re looking for exceptional talent to help us move even faster.position summarywe're looking for someone who understands the software delivery problem at a technical level and can translate it into clear, compelling content for the audiences who care most about solving it — developers, engineering and security leaders, and the broader tech community following where enterprise software is headed.this role sits at the intersection of technology, communication, and market narrative. you'll develop a deep understanding of what harness is building and translate that — alongside what's happening across the industry — into content that earns attention from a technical audience.reporting to the vp of corporate marketing, this role will partner directly with the executive team at harness and work cross-functionally with engineering, product management, and marketing to ensure harness's point of view is grounded in what we're buildingabout the roleyou'll develop content that represents harness's point of view — substantive technical and industry commentary that reflects how practitioners actually think about software delivery, ai governance, security, developer productivity, and engineering roi.that means staying current on what's being published, debated, and shipped across the industry. reading the pragmatic engineer, tracking what engineering leaders are saying, knowing when a dora report or a vc thesis or a major industry announcement is something worth responding to. then translating harness's actual position into words quickly — before the conversation moves on.day to day, you'll monitor the news and developer conversation, identify what's worth engaging with, develop angles and post ideas, write and refine content across linkedin, x, and other external platforms, and iterate quickly based on feedback. you'll work closely with communications and marketing but operate with real ownership over detail.desc: about audubonthe national audubon society is a leading nonprofit conservation organization with 120 years of science-based, community-driven impact, dedicated to protecting birds and the places they need, today and tomorrow. birds are powerful indicators of our planet’s health, acting as sentinels that warn us of environmental change and inspire action. audubon works across the western hemisphere, driven by the understanding that what is good for birds is good for the planet. through a collaborative, nonpartisan approach across habitats, borders, and the political spectrum, audubon drives meaningful and lasting conservation outcomes. with over 1,000 staff and more than 2.6 million supporters, audubon is a dynamic and ever-growing force committed to ensuring a better planet for both birds and people for generations to come. learn more at audubon.org and on facebook and instagram @audubonsociety.position summaryaudubon's conservation impact depends not only on the work the organization leads, but on how that work is understood, embraced, and acted upon by the audiences who can help advance it—from policymakers and partners to supporters, employees, and communities across the hemisphere. reporting to the senior director of internal communications, this senior manager role helps shape audubon's voice on the issues that define its mission and helps advance the flight plan priorities that guide the organization's hemispheric work.a core member of the communications team, the position collaborates primarily with the office of the chief conservation officer (occo) to ensure communications activity is integrated, strategic, and enterprise-focused. the role brings strategic judgment, strong writing, and a collaborative approach to a fast-paced, mission-driven environment, and aims to drive consistency, impact, and forward momentum. the role will support communications priorities—including executive communications, organizational change, internal communications, and other strategic initiatives—as needed, consistent with the communications department's enterprise approach.this position is classified as hybrid, in accordance with audubon’s “where we work” policy. hybrid employees are expected to work in an audubon office every monday and tuesday and an additional two days each month of the employee’s choosing. candidates washington, dc$118,890 - $133,751 / year = new york, ny; oakland, ca additional job descriptionessential functions:partnering with leadership for the development and execution of communications the americas, and cross-functional leaders within audubon to ensure communications are integrated, strategic, and enterprise-focused.identifies and secures high-level opportunities for leadership to participate in conferences, speaking engagements, media appearances, and other strategic engagements, ensuring alignment with audubon’s broader communications strategies.ensures alignment between communications from the office of the chief conservation officer with broader organizational priorities, supporting proactive internal communications, executive communications, organizational change initiatives, the chief conservation officer’s thought leadership strategy, and consistent enterprise messaging.regularly monitors emerging trends in conservation, policy, and communications to ensure detail.desc: the american cancer society cancer action network (acs can) is the nation's leading cancer advocacy organization. together with our charitable partner, the american cancer society, we work in congress, state legislatures and local jurisdictions to support evidence-based policy and legislative solutions designed to eliminate cancer as a major health problem.leads media advocacy efforts for assigned territory of arkansas, florida, louisiana, texas, oklahoma and puerto rico, both in english and spanish, providing input into campaign planning, implementing tactics to support policy and revenue activities, driving relevance, and enhancing acs can brand recognition in support of local, state, and federal priorities. provides a full range of media outreach, including developing target media lists and building relationships with key capitol press corps, health reporters and diverse news outlets. drafts talking points, fact sheets, news releases/advisories as well as opinion editorial articles and letters to the editor. secures editorial meetings and earned media placement by leveraging digital media skills and selling story ideas by phone and electronically to print, radio and tv newsrooms.***candidates must be home based in one of these following states/territories: arkansas, florida, louisiana, texas, oklahoma and puerto rico. must be a strong communicator with excellent writing and verbal skills in english and spanish. prior experience with legislative and advocacy campaign experience is highly preferred. ***essential functions:assist in drafting and implementation of strategic media advocacy plans for local, state and federal policy campaigns, to demonstrate broad based public support for cancer-related policy initiatives. assist in occasional ballot and electoral campaign planning. draft and implement such plans directly, in assigned multi state geography of arkansas, florida, louisiana, texas, oklahoma and puerto rico. (30%) develop messaging that is tailored to the specific political environment and attuned to the rapid pace of legislative activities. write and coach others to enhance their writing of press releases, media advisories, letters to the editor, op-eds, talking points, faqs, fact sheets, speeches, presentations and other media material as needed, ensuring appropriate review for subject matter accuracy and brand standards. plan and manage media events, including press conferences and editorial board meetings. (30%) develop and maintain relationships with press corps in assigned multi state geography, and proactively engage these reporters on legislative issues as well as responding to media inquiries. track and report media results and trends. (20%) coordinate activities with acs marketing & communications staff, as well as with acs can media advocacy colleagues as needed. manage media activities to support acs can fundraising. (5%) represent acs can in coalitions for priority campaigns to ensure coordination and brand recognition with joint media activities (5%) elevate the profile of acs can, by working through the media to ensure that opinion leaders are aware of acs can legislative activity and voter education activity. who we areclean air task force (catf) is a global nonprofit organization working to safeguard against the worst impacts of climate change by catalyzing the rapid development and deployment of low-carbon energy and other climate-protecting technologies. with 30 years of internationally recognized expertise on climate policy and a fierce commitment to exploring all potential solutions, catf is a pragmatic, non-ideological advocacy group with the bold ideas needed to address climate change. catf has offices in boston, washington, d.c., and brussels, with staff working virtually around the world.what you'll docatf works to accelerate the solutions needed to achieve a zero-emissions future. as a senior leader within the communications & marketing team, you will shape how catf tells its story, elevates its ideas and experts, and engages the audiences that can help turn climate and energy solutions into real-world impact.you will bring together institutional storytelling, executive communications, strategic events, media relations, and other important communications opportunities. working across catf, you will help determine which stories we tell, where and how we show up, and how our communications support organizational priorities.this role will build an integrated editorial and engagement strategy that connects catf's expertise with policymakers, industry leaders, donors, media, and other influential audiences.responsibilitieseditorial strategy & institutional storytelling – develop and carry out catf's organization-wide editorial strategy and content calendar, turning organizational priorities and technical expertise into clear, compelling stories for priority audiences.messaging, voice & editorial standards – maintain catf's organizational messaging, editorial standards, voice, and style guidance so communications are accurate, accessible, consistent, and aligned with catf's brand.flagship content leadership – lead or guide major institutional content, including catf's annual report, organizational and program milestones, impact case studies, and other high-profile content.strategic events & external engagement – develop an organization-wide approach to priority events and engagements, including conferences, climate weeks, convenings, speaking opportunities, roundtables, executive engagements, and catf-led events. help determine the audience, messaging, speakers, content, and communications strategy for each opportunity.executive communications & thought leadership – develop communications strategies for catf executives and senior experts. identify opportunities and produce speeches, opinion pieces, commentary, presentations, talking points, and other executive communications.media relations & reputation building – work with communications & marketing colleagues to build relationships with influential journalists and outlets, elevate catf's experts, and provide communications counsel during major media moments and sensitive or reputational issues.integrated content & engagement planning – connect catf's editorial, media, executive communications, and event strategies through an integrated planning process tied to organizational priorities and audience needs.people leadership & team development – supervise, coach, and develop communications staff. set clear priorities and standards while supporting independent judgment, collaboration, and professional growth.what you'll bringyou are an experienced communications leader, writer, editor, convener, and strategist who understands how strong ideas become useful stories, conversations, and engagements. you can make complex climate, energy, technical, and policy issues clear without losing important context.you bring sound editorial judgment and a collaborative leadership style. you can advise senior leaders, develop staff, and build alignment across functions, cultures, geographies, and time zones.required experiencebachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.10–15 years of progressively responsible experience in strategic communications, editorial leadership, media relations, journalism, public affairs, external engagement, or a related field.strong english-language writing, editing, and storytelling skills, including experience translating complex technical or policy issues into clear communications.demonstrated expertise in editorial strategy, institutional storytelling, organizational messaging, and high-profile content.significant experience developing executive communications and thought leadership, including speeches, opinion pieces, commentary, presentations, talking points, or other executive-level content.experience developing proactive media relations strategies, working directly with journalists and editors, and advising on sensitive, rapid-response, or reputational communications.experience developing strategic events and external engagements, including conferences, convenings, executive engagements, speaking opportunities, or similar forums.people leadership and cross-functional collaboration experience, including supervising and developing staff, advising senior leaders, and working with technical experts, policy professionals, development teams, and communications colleagues.preferred major international climate, energy, policy, business, or philanthropic forums.experience developing editorial or event content for donors, funders, and other philanthropic audiences.experience working in a global or geographically distributed organization.experience in a nonprofit, think tank, research institution, philanthropic organization, government, journalism, or a similarly mission-driven environment.additional language skills.what we providejoin a team working to accelerate climate solutions while improving how catf shares its work and engages the audiences that can technology, energy, and policy issues.cross-functional work with communications & marketing, development, executive leadership, and catf's programs and regions.a collaborative and intellectually curious culture where diverse perspectives are valued and bold, practical solutions to climate change are encouraged.a flexible remote working environment, with a preference for candidates based in the united states and the ability to work effectively across u.s. and european time zones.periodic domestic and international travel for catf meetings, conferences, strategic events, media opportunities, and other organizational priorities.benefits designed to support health, financial security, time away, and flexibility.compensation & pay transparencycatf believes candidates should tennesseans for student successtennesseans for student success (tss) champions effective education policies that give every tennessee child access to a quality public education. we combine data, political impact, and the collective power of parents, advocates, and policymakers to make tennessee the gold standard in public education and to hold leaders accountable for student outcomes.building power. leveraging influence. changing student lives.tss is hiring a director of external affairs to own the organization's voice across every channel, earned media, owned media, social, podcast, and our flagship digital outlet. this is not a traditional communications role, and it is not a newsroom role.we are looking for a strategist and operator who sees communications as an advocacy function that drive public opinion and outcomes: someone who can build narratives that move tennesseans, legislators, and the policy influencers; produce content that performs across formats; and lead a small team toward measurable advocacy outcomes. the right person thinks like a marketer, writes like a journalist, moves like a campaign comms director, and treats the flagship digital outlet as a powerful platform to advance tss's policy and political priorities, not as a traditional newsroom operating in a vacuum.this role reports to executive leadership and manages the communications function, including editorial operations, contractors, and vendors.what you'll ownstrategic direction for a digital news outlet serve as managing editor, setting the editorial vision, content calendar, and growth strategy in alignment with tss's policy and political objectives.build the outlet into a multi-format platform: articles, podcast, video, social-first content, newsletters, that drives audience growth and shapes the education narrative in tennessee.define and track performance metrics: audience growth, engagement, share of voice, narrative penetration, and influence on key audiences (parents, legislators, opinion leaders).make sharp editorial calls: on story selection, framing, headlines, distribution, and rapid response, that maximize the platform's strategic value.integrated communications & brandlead tss's full communications strategy and daily operations across earned, owned, and paid channels.develop and enforce organizational messaging, ensuring consistency across tss, digital news outlet, and affiliated entities.draft, edit, and approve press releases, op-eds, talking points, newsletters, and public statements.oversee brand identity, voice, and visual consistency across every public-facing asset.digital, social & multimediadirect the social media strategy across all platforms, with a marketer's eye for reach, engagement, and conversion, not just posting.oversee podcast development, production cadence, guest strategy, and distribution.manage email marketing and audience-building programs to grow and activate tss supporter lists.use analytics to continuously iterate on what's working, and kill what isn't.earned media & public relationsserve as the organization's primary media contact and build relationships with reporters, editors, and producers statewide and nationally.pitch stories, place op-eds, coordinate interviews, and prepare leadership for media engagements.monitor media coverage and respond quickly and effectively, including in contested or politically charged moments.political & electoral communicationspartner with the political and policy teams to develop sharp, accurate, and well-sourced content during legislative sessions, election cycles, and accountability campaigns.lead rapid-response messaging when tss's priorities, allies, or interests are under attack, or when opportunities to advance them emerge.translate complex policy and political dynamics into clear, persuasive content built for the audience and channel.team & operations•      manage communications staff, the editorial team, freelance contributors, and external vendors.•      set goals, workflows, and performance expectations; develop talent and elevate the team's work.•      manage budgets, vendor relationships, and project timelines.•      support crisis communications planning and response.who you arewe are intentionally looking outside the traditional journalism mold. strong candidates will bring:5+ years in communications, marketing, political/campaign communications, advocacy, or a hybrid of these, with measurable results.a modern, audience-first mindset: you understand how content actually travels in 2026, across social, podcast, video, and email, not just press releases.marketing instincts. you think in terms of audience, message, channel, and conversion, and you know how to measure what's working.editorial chops. you can write fast and cleanly, edit other people's work to a high standard, and confidently call on framing, headlines, and story selection.political and advocacy fluency. you're comfortable operating in a mission-driven, electorally active environment and understand how communications drives policy and political outcomes.multi-format range: comfortable shaping a podcast episode, a reels script, a long-form op-ed, and a rapid-response thread, or directing others to.strategic thinking paired with a builder's mentality. you can write a 12-month strategic plan this is a public-facing role in a politically active organization.nice to have•      experience with a political campaign, 501(c)(4), pac, or advocacy organization.•      experience launching or scaling a podcast, newsletter, or digital media property.•      crisis communications experience.•      graphic design, video production, or content creation skills.•      familiarity with media monitoring tools, crm/email platforms, and social analytics.•      bachelor's degree in communications, marketing, political science, public relations, journalism, or a related field. equivalent professional experience considered.logistics•      full-time, salaried.•      based in franklin, tn. in-office three days per week.•      approximately 25% travel within tennessee.•      some evening and weekend work for events, breaking news, and political moments.•      must have a valid driver's license and access to a personal vehicle for work travel.compensation & benefitscompetitive salary commensurate with experience, plus a strong benefits package:•      employer-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance•      flexible spending accounts (fsa) and health savings account (hsa) options•      immediate eligibility for 401(k) with employer match•      paid parental leave (maternity, paternity, adoption)•      flexible pto and paid federal and organizational
