detail.desc: summary job summary cu boulder encourages applications for an associate director of digital strategy! this role is responsible for developing and implementing the social media strategy of colorado athletics with a primary focus on colorado women’s basketball. this position will play a key role in elevating the program's digital presence through creative storytelling, social media management, photography, graphic design, and short-form video production.working collaboratively with the creative services team, women's basketball staff, and athletics communications and marketing, this position will create compelling, platform-specific content that showcases student-athletes, coaches, team culture, and the overall colorado women's basketball brand along with any other program assigned by the director of digital strategy.the associate director will take point in managing the program's official social media accounts, developing content calendars, assist in producing original creative assets, and providing coverage of games, practices, team activities, recruiting initiatives, and special events. this individual should be highly creative, organized, and comfortable working in a fast-paced collegiate athletics environment.the successful candidate will have a strong understanding of emerging social media trends, digital storytelling, with the ability to capture, edit, and publish engaging content across multiple platforms.this position is responsible for promoting the philosophy and objectives of the intercollegiate athletics program, including adherence to the athletic department's mission statement, core values, policies and procedures, and the rules and regulations of the university, big 12 conference, and ncaa.cu is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment. we are committed to creating a workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and dignity, and we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply, including protected veterans and individuals with disabilities.who we areas one of 34 u.s. public research institutions belonging to the prestigious association of american universities (aau)—and the only member in the rocky mountain region—our goal at cu boulder is to directly affect colorado communities through collaborative research, innovation, and entrepreneurship. our faculty, staff, and students work with the broader community to establish outstanding connections that have lasting outcomes—both across colorado and around the world.responsibilities what your key responsibilities will be social media management and strategymanage the day-to-day operations of colorado women's basketball's official social media accounts, including instagram, x, tiktok, facebook, and emerging platforms.assist in running the main account of athletics as assigned by the director of digital strategy.develop and implement engaging social media content that increases visibility, audience engagement, and brand awareness for the women's basketball program and other sports as assigned.create and maintain comprehensive social media content calendars that align with team's schedules, promotional initiatives, and overall departmental strategy.provide real-time social media coverage of games, practices, press conferences, team events, and other basketball-related activities.develop creative concepts and social-first storytelling initiatives that highlight student-athletes, coaches, team accomplishments, and program culture.identify and incorporate emerging social media trends, platform features, and standard processes to keep the program's digital presence relevant and engaging.monitor audience engagement, platform performance, and content effectiveness to identify opportunities for growth.maintain consistency with colorado athletics branding, messaging, and social media standards.digital content creation and productioncapture, produce, and edit original short-form video content for social media platforms, including instagram reels, tiktok, and other digital channels.assist in graphic design and photography needs in collaboration with the graphic design team within creative services.lead recruiting visit media days and assist in content collection.collaborate with the creative services team on content concepts, visual direction, and production needs.assist with content that supports student-athlete personal branding and name, image, and likeness (nil) storytelling initiatives.organize and maintain digital content assets, including photography, video footage, and graphics.content planning and program supportcollaborate with women's basketball staff and assigned programs to identify storytelling opportunities and develop content that supports the program's overall brand and recruiting initiatives.work closely with athletics communications, marketing, and creative services to coordinate content coverage and promotional efforts.assist coaching staffs in recruiting calendar and supporting creative assets needed in recruitment of student athletes.assist in developing digital campaigns that promote games, ticket sales, fan engagement, community outreach, and special events.support content needs related to recruiting visits, team announcements, student-athlete features, and program landmarks, in accordance with applicable ncaa and institutional policies.help coordinate content production schedules and ensure timely delivery of digital assets.collaborate with student-athletes and coaches to develop authentic and engaging social media content.analytics and digital engagement track social media performance, including audience growth, engagement, reach, and content effectiveness.assist in evaluating social media trends and analytics to improve content performance.find opportunities to increase engagement and expand the women's basketball program, athletics account and other programs as assigned.work closely with student athletes to grow personal brand and collaborate centrally within cu athletics.provide periodic social media performance updates and content recommendations.monitor platform developments and recommend creative approaches to digital storytelling.what you should knowthis position will be working in-person.evenings, weekends, and holidays may be required depending on business needs. what we can offer$70,900 - $75,000. relocation assistance is available within athletics department guidelines.athletic event tickets: per athletic department policy and ncaa regulationsnike elite employee benefit: per nike elite policysupplemental camp pay: per athletic department summer camp policybenefitsat the university of colorado boulder , we are committed to supporting the holistic health and well-being of our employees. our comprehensive benefits package includes medical, dental, and retirement plans; generous paid time off; tuition assistance for you and your dependents; and an eco pass for local transit. as one of boulder county’s largest employers, cu boulder offers an inspiring academic community and access to world-class outdoor recreation. in fact, cu boulder has been named one of forbes' america's best large employers , ranking #4 among large employers in colorado and #28 among universities nationwide. explore additional perks and programs through the cu advantage program. be statements be ambitious. be groundbreaking. be boulder.what we requirebachelor's degree (or equivalent experience) in communications, journalism, digital media, marketing, graphic design, sports management, or a related field. equivalent combination of education and experience may substitute.three (3) years experience in social media management, digital content creation, photography, video production, graphic design, or a related field. experience using video editing, graphic design, or photography software. familiarity with major social media platforms and current digital content trends. demonstrated ability to create and publish engaging social media content.what you will needstrong understanding of social media platforms, including instagram, tiktok, x, and facebook.ability to capture and edit short-form video content specifically designed for social media.working knowledge of photography, camera equipment, and basic photo editing techniques.proficiency with adobe creative cloud, including photoshop, premiere pro, lightroom, or similar creative software.ability to design engaging social media graphics consistent with established brand standards.strong creative storytelling skills and an understanding of sports-related digital content.ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced athletics environment.phenomenal organizational skills and ability to manage multiple projects with set timelines.excellent written and verbal communication skills.willingness and ability to work evenings, weekends, and selected travel dates associated with athletic competitions and events.what we would like you to haveexperience creating digital content for a collegiate or professional athletics program.experience managing social media accounts for a sports team, brand, or organization.demonstrated portfolio of short-form video production, photography, and graphic design work.experience capturing live sports photography and video content.knowledge of women's basketball and the collegiate athletics landscape.experience developing creative content featuring student-athletes and coaches.proven success growing social media audiences and increasing engagement.familiarity with ncaa, conference, and institutional policies related to athletics communications and social media. special instructions to apply, please submit the following materialsa current resume. a cover letter that specifically tells us how your background and experience align with the requirements, qualifications, and responsibilities of the position. we may request references at a later time.please apply by 11/11/26 for consideration.note: application materials will not be accepted via email. for consideration, please apply through cu boulder jobs .in compliance with the colorado job application fairness act, in any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school attendance or graduation. you will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information.essential servicesthis position is designated “essential/critical services.” the incumbent is required to respond to requests for work during campus emergencies (snow, wind, rain, flood and any other natural or man-made event) and report to work for regularly assigned shifts during emergency campus closures.

company summaryat usa triathlon, we believe in the power of sport to transform lives, and in the strength of a team that lives that passion and mission every day. as the olympic and paralympic national governing body (ngb) for triathlon and multisport in the u.s., we’re driven to grow participation, inspire communities, and empower athletes of all backgrounds to reach their personal bests.we’re a team of bold thinkers, passionate doers, and collaborative leaders united by service, performance, innovation, and inclusion. recognized by the u.s. olympic & paralympic committee for our commitment to diversity and inclusion, we offer unlimited pto, 100% employer-paid medical benefits, and a supportive culture that celebrates excellence and balance.every day, our work is fueled by our purpose, mission, and vision: purpose: give everyone a chance to tri: removing barriers and creating opportunities for all. mission: drive success for multisport from the starting line to lifelong love. vision: bring triathlon to new places, people, and possibilities.we’re the hub for a nationwide multisport community of athletes, coaches, race directors, and clubs. from youth and collegiate development to supporting the core of our grassroots racing community and high-performance programming building to olympic and paralympic games, usa triathlon drives the future of endurance sport in america.position summaryusa triathlon is hiring an email & audience communications manager to own our most direct line to the community. email is how more than 300,000+ members, and the athletes, coaches, race directors, clubs, donors and fans around them, engage with our greater sports ecosystem, register for key events, understand benefits of membership, follow usa tri, give to the foundation and stay connected to the sport across usa triathlon, usa tri and the usa triathlon foundation.on the growth marketing team, you’ll lead email campaigns for our biggest moments, from championships and registration openings to giving days and the la 2028 games, and own every newsletter and required communication we send. success is measured by outcomes: registrations, memberships, donations, purchases and an engaged audience. this role fits someone who loves the craft of email, cares about the details, and builds processes that keep a high-volume program accurate and on time.essential job functionslead campaigns for our biggest moments. plan and run email campaigns that drive registrations and participation for national championships, endurance exchange, other series and sanctioned events, plus membership drives, giving days and la 2028 moments. partner with events, philanthropy, corporate partnerships, the content team and the growth & lifecycle manager from plan to results.own every newsletter. plan, build and deploy the full portfolio, including the membership, club, coaches, age group team usa, race director and foundation newsletters, and make each one worth opening. maintain templates and modules within brand standards set with creative services.own required and compliance communications. deploy legal, policy and compliance sends accurately and on deadline with the correct send classification. partner with legal on approvals and keep a clear record of what was sent, to whom and when.own the calendar and every send. manage the email calendar in line with marketing operations’ campaign calendar, planning ahead of renewals, championships, registration deadlines, giving days and the olympic and paralympic calendar. build and deploy in salesforce marketing cloud, with qa built into every send through checklists, test sends and peer review.build and engage our audiences. build audiences from salesforce crm and membership data, sharpen segmentation, and expand personalization with dynamic content and ampscript. grow opt-ins and win back lapsed subscribers.improve how we work. document and strengthen workflows, templates and qa standards, and cut manual work as volume grows. when something goes wrong, fix it quickly, communicate clearly and update the process.write for the inbox. turn stories from the content team into email, with subject lines, preheaders and copy in the brand voice that get people to open and act.test and measure outcomes. run ongoing a/b tests on subject lines, content, layout, send time and frequency, and roll winners into standards. tie email to registrations, memberships, donations and purchases, feed marketing operations dashboards, and turn results into recommendations.protect list health and governance. set frequency rules, send priority and preference management. monitor inbox placement, bounces, complaints and unsubscribes; manage authentication, suppression and list hygiene; and comply with can-spam, casl, privacy requirements and usopc, ioc and ipc rules, including rule 40.supervisory responsibilitiesnone. may coordinate contractors and cross-functional contributors on email deliverables.knowledge, skills, and abilitiessalesforce marketing cloud expertise. hands-on with email studio, content builder, automation studio, journey builder, data extensions.technical fluency. sql for segmentation, ampscript for personalization, and html and css for email.detail orientation. catches small things early, builds checks into the process, and learns from mistakes.campaign thinking. plans multi-send campaigns around a goal and a deadline across teams.audience empathy. writes for the real person behind each send, from first-time racer to donor.segmentation and testing. builds relevant audiences from crm data and ties tests to conversions and revenue.email copywriting. sharp subject lines, preheaders and copy that drive action in the brand’s voice.deliverability. understands sender reputation, authentication (spf, dkim, dmarc), list hygiene and inbox placement.organization and communication. manages many sends, stakeholders and deadlines at once; documents processes; explains technical issues in plain language and holds the line on governance.qualifications4–6+ years of hands-on email marketing, including at least 2 years in salesforce marketing cloud or a comparable platform.a track record running a high-volume program accurately and on schedule, including campaigns tied to registration, sales or fundraising goals.experience with sql, data extensions, ampscript, dynamic content and crm data, ideally salesforce crm and marketing cloud connect.experience managing deliverability and list health, and measuring email’s impact on conversions and revenue through a/b testing.strong email copywriting skills; writing samples required.strong project management across multiple priorities and stakeholders in a lean environment.preferredsalesforce marketing cloud email specialist or administrator certification.email experience with a membership organization, nonprofit or sports property, including fundraising or sponsorship programs.experience with sms or other audience channels, and familiarity with endurance or participation-based sport.working conditions and physical requirementsusa triathlon offers a hybrid work schedule and requires this position to be on site at usat headquarters in colorado springs, co at least two days per weekwhile performing the duties of this job, the employee may be regularly required to stand, sit, talk, hear, reach, stoop, kneel, and use hands and fingers to operate a computer, telephone, and keyboard. the employee may be required to exert force to manipulate or move items weighing up to 30 pounds.this position may require limited non-traditional work hours including evenings, weekends, and some holidays related to usa triathlon event attendance and support. event attendance and support may entail travel, including outside of traditional office hours, to usa triathlon events and/or international eventseeo statementusa triathlon is an equal opportunity employer. all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status.disclaimerthis job description is intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed. it is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, and qualifications required. duties and responsibilities may change as business needs evolve.

company descriptionsarah hall productions, inc. is an award-winning boutique pr & social media firm specializing in lifestyle & entertainment accounts. with more than 30 years of experience, sarah and her team have built a reputation based on their attention to detail and unswerving dedication to clients. clients include celebrity athletes, authors, designers, doctors, fashion, fitness gurus, food, product lines, and personal growth and wellness experts.role descriptionwe’re seeking a highly motivated and media-savvy publicist to join our dynamic team. this role is ideal for a pr professional with 2–3 years of agency or in-house experience who’s eager to take ownership of day-to-day media outreach and contribute to strategic campaigns across our lifestyle, entertainment, and wellness accounts.as a publicist, you’ll be responsible for drafting and pitching compelling stories to the media while building and maintaining media relationships. you will support high-profile client campaigns from concept through execution.this is a fantastic opportunity to take the next step in your pr career, gaining hands-on experience in a fast-paced, collaborative agency environment.this is a full-time, on-site role located in nyc. we are in office 5 days/week. this is not a hybrid or wfh position. do not apply if you do not live in nyc.salary is based on experience.qualifications·     2–3 years of pr experience (agency or in-house preferred)·     excellent communication skills·     proven experience pitching media and securing placements·     highly organized, detail-oriented, and deadline-driven·     passion for storytelling, pop culture, and media·     positive attitude, team-oriented, and eager to grow·     experience with social media and digital marketing is a plus·   able to work well under pressure and tight deadlinesvisit our website www.shpny.com to check us out!

wild places. through science, advocacy and partnerships with communities and policymakers, we champion the protection of wilderness, national parks, forests, and other public lands that provide clean air and water, wildlife habitat and the freedom to connect with nature. for more information, visit www.wilderness.org.position overviewthe communications manager develops and executes advocacy communications strategies that advance the organization’s priorities, strengthen its public narrative, and increase the impact and reach of its work. working closely with program, policy, legal, government relations, digital, and other teams, this person leads communications planning, message development, and earned media strategy, while helping plan and guide digital content development for arctic campaigns in alaska and place-based work in western states. the role also includes preparing spokespeople, developing compelling stories and communications materials, and collaborating with internal teams and external partners to engage priority audiences and advance advocacy goals. because approximately 50 percent of the role supports alaska campaigns, the person must have a strong understanding of the state’s politics, people, and landscape.this position plays a critical role in fostering an organizational culture where people feel respected, included, and accountable to shared goals and outcomes. tws has made it a priority to ensure that our public lands work reflects fairness, representation, and accessibility. this role will carry those commitments into our external affairs work—expanding partnerships, strengthening community connections, and ensuring our work is responsive to a broad range of perspectives and needs. across our team, we aspire to be campaign-oriented, collaborative, innovative, transparent, and supportive of staff – our greatest asset.essential duties and responsibilities develop long-term, proactive communication strategies and plans to reach priority audiences and achieve intended impact across paid, owned, and earned media.coordinate work and monitor progress towards tws metrics, milestones, and outcomes. ensure content lives in one central location that can be accessed by the full team.review and offer strategic input and counsel on broader narratives, priorities and plans, including leading the development of communications outreach for initiatives focused on alaska and other state(s).lead narrative creation and messaging oversight for the arctic, western arctic and ambler road campaigns as well as place-based campaigns in western states. this includes creating overarching narratives, press statements, talking points, memos, reports, and other communications resources.ensure messaging is consistent across channels, position tws as a thought leader, and supports paid, owned, and earned media goals.work closely with digital colleagues to support the development of compelling, audience-focused content for websites, email, membership communications, social media, and other digital platforms, ensuring alignment with campaign narratives, messaging strategies, and organizational goals.execute both national and local media relations related to portfolio of work including hosting media events, pitching stories, drafting releases, and shaping of narrative with journalists.cultivate new reporter relationships that reach and influence target audiences. shares contacts with other communicators as appropriate.prepare and train tws and partner spokespeople for interviews, events, and testimony, and develop speeches, talking points, written testimony, and other materials that advance campaign priorities.coordinate media relations and external communications with relevant tws teams to ensure alignment on messaging, priorities, and opportunities.collaborate with the membership team to identify opportunities to engage, educate, and fundraise with tws members.participate in coalition efforts, providing communications expertise and support to partners as needed. build and maintain relationships with partners who can help tell compelling stories about the importance and impact of tws's work.collaborate on larger creative initiatives, including film launches, webinars, reports, story maps, and other storytelling opportunities, ensuring content aligns with organizational narratives and campaign priorities.qualificationsexperience, competencies, and educationminimum 5 years’ experience in communications, content creation, external affairs, public relations, and/or marketing.strong understanding of the alaska's politics, people, and landscape preferred.track record working successfully in teams representing a rich mix of talent, backgrounds, and perspectives.strong experience working with members of the press and a solid understanding of the media landscape, both local and national media.strong understanding of social media and writing, and producing content for digital audiences.strong understanding of the legislative process at the state and federal level.proven ability to evaluate and analyze legislation and/or other policy solutions for understanding and alignment with organizational positions and values.excellent written and verbal communications skills, including the ability to translate complex policies succinctly and clearly for a public audience and decision makers.proven ability to develop strategies and tactics to achieve an advocacy goal.strong understanding of holistic, behavior-change communications and the ability to strategically design communication plans that are comprehensive and impactful to targeted audiences.strong problem-solving skills and careful attention to detail. solution-orientation mindset.a good understanding of or experience in crafting strategies that include values-based audience targeting and tailoring messaging accordingly.familiarity, sensitivity to and/or experience working with indigenous communities and/or sovereign tribal nations.commitment to and experience with ethical storytelling.understanding and commitment to advancing equity and justice in the policy-making process. experience working with coalitions focused on environmental and/or social justice issues preferred.this job description is intended to convey information essential to understanding the scope of this position and it is not intended to be an exhaustive list of experience, skills, efforts, duties, responsibilities or working conditions associated with the position.this position could be performed remotely or from a tws office (where applicable) in the following states: ak, ca, wa, mt, id, nv, ut or co. the salary range for this position is $80,000-$95,000 depending on location and experience. to apply, please submit resume and cover letter by november 29th, 2026.the wilderness society offers a competitive salary and benefits package, including health, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, and pet insurance; sick and vacation leave; a sabbatical program; and a retirement plan with employer contribution subject to certain limits and requirements. tws is an equal opportunity employer and actively works to ensure fair treatment of our employees and constituents across culture, socioeconomic status, race, marital or family situation, gender, age, ethnicity, religious beliefs, physical ability, veteran status or sexual orientation.as an organization, we aspire to being inclusive in the work that we do, and in the kind of organization we are.internally, this means working as a team that listens to different points of view, recognizes the contributions of every employee and empowers each employee to bring their whole selves to work every day. externally, this means ensuring that public lands are inclusive and welcoming, so that our shared wildlands can help people and nature to thrive. we are committed to equity throughout our work, which we define as our commitment to realizing the promise of our public lands and ensuring that all can share in their universal benefits. to learn more about our commitment, please see http://wilderness.org/our-commitment-diversity-equity-and-inclusion-wilderness-society pursuant to applicable fair chance laws, tws will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.tws complies with federal and state disability laws and is committed to providing reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities. if you about vincievery so often, a company emerges with the technology, momentum, and ambition to change an entire industry. for the right communications leader, joining at that moment can be career-defining. vinci is at that moment.we're tackling one of the biggest challenges in technology: the growing gap between the complexity of the hardware the world needs and our ability to understand how it will actually work before it's built. as ai accelerates demand for more powerful chips and increasingly sophisticated electronic systems, traditional engineering tools are struggling to keep pace. it's one of the defining challenges of the ai era—and vinci has a breakthrough solution that's already generating coverage in the technology and business press, along with engagement with leading journalists and podcasters.we've pioneered the physics intelligence platform, bringing ai-native physics computation to hardware engineering. instead of waiting days or weeks for answers, engineers can understand the physical consequences of their designs in seconds to minutes, explore vastly more alternatives, and discover better solutions. this isn't another incremental improvement to engineering software. it's a new computational capability with the potential to transform how the world's most advanced hardware is designed.and this isn't just a vision. vinci's technology has been adopted across more than 40 engineering programs at some of the world's leading semiconductor and electronics companies. we've just raised a $250 million series b at a $1.5 billion valuation, backed by some of the world's most respected investors. the technology is real, the customer adoption is real, and the market opportunity is enormous.now comes the opportunity to tell that story to the world.you'll have direct access to a highly engaged executive team that understands the power of communications and wants to invest in it. you'll work with extraordinary technical talent, leading customers, strategic partners, and a growing body of evidence that gives journalists, analysts, and industry influencers something genuinely newsworthy to talk about.this is not a place where communications waits for permission to be interesting. we're building a company that moves quickly, thinks ambitiously, and wants its communications team to do the same. you'll have the freedom to experiment, the resources to execute, and the opportunity to help establish a new category while the market is still learning its name.if you've ever wanted to join a breakthrough technology company just as the world begins to discover it—and help shape what the world thinks about it—this is that opportunity.role overviewwe want to build a communications machine that punches far above its weight—and we're looking for someone with the ambition, creativity, and drive to help build it.not a traditional pr and social media operation. a fast-moving, ai-powered engine that turns breakthrough technology, customer successes, executive insights, and industry developments into a continuous stream of stories and conversations that shape the market.our ambition is to own the conversation around physics intelligence. to make vinci a company journalists want to cover, podcasters want to interview, industry leaders want to engage with, and engineers want to follow. we want to move faster, experiment more boldly, and generate more influence than companies with communications teams many times our size.you'll help orchestrate an integrated communications program spanning social media, ai not simply to produce content faster, but to rethink how a small team can achieve extraordinary reach and influence.this is a hands-on builder's role based in our palo alto office. you'll work closely with the head of corporate marketing, product marketing, our communications agency, and content factory, with direct access to the executives and technical experts whose ideas you'll bring to loot labs is on a mission to make collecting fun. we believe that every collectible tells a story: of passion, nostalgia, and discovery.through our flagship product, boxed.gg we are reimagining how the world collects by blending digital entertainment with tangible rewards, delivering nostalgia and discovery straight to the fans' doorsteps.we are...community first: we've served 1m collectors and foster an active community of over 145k+ discord members. ambitiously led: led by veterans from microsoft, twitch, 2k, and boeing. remote-first: we value high autonomy, low ego, and trust our team to build from anywhere in the world. since our inception in 2023, we’ve seen significant year-over-year growth. and now we're gearing up for our most ambitious year yet, with major expansions planned across product offerings, strategic partnerships, and next-generation collector experiences. if you’re ready to build products that spark joy at a global scale, you’re in the right place.role descriptionreporting to the content lead, the social media manager owns boxed's social channels and turns attention from collectors into new users. your job is to make boxed the account the hobby actually follows: fast, native to collector culture, on-trend, and unmistakably ours.reach matters, but it isn't the scoreboard. social is an acquisition channel for us, and your work should show up in signups, app installs, and first purchases. you'll write, shoot, edit, and post yourself, and build the systems, partners, and creator sources that let output scale beyond what one person can make.in your first year, success means social is a measurable acquisition channel: signups, installs, and first purchases attributed to owned social every month and growing quarter over quarter, a real hobby audience across both tcg and sports, and a steady pipeline of proven formats feeding paid creative.key responsibilitieschannel strategy - own day-to-day strategy, publishing, and performance across tiktok, youtube (including shorts), instagram, x, and reddit, with a distinct playbook for each. trend spotting - catch trends, sounds, memes, and hobby moments early, and get on-brand content live the same day while they're still rising. content creation - write, shoot, and edit native short-form content, and develop recurring series such as pack openings, pull reactions, hobby explainers, and community spotlights. user acquisition - drive signups, app installs, first purchases, and referral activity from social, and test calls to action and conversion paths from content to product. measurement - work with growth and analytics on attribution (utms, link-in-bio, promo codes, app deep links) and report acquisition by channel, not just reach. sports audience - grow the sports card audience with the same intent as tcg. team collaboration - partner with influencer, field, and community teams to amplify creator content, turn cons and nationals into a month of posts, and promote the referral program and discord. qualificationsexperience: 3+ years running social for a consumer brand, app, or media company, with a track record of growing an audience and tying it to signups, installs, or revenue. editorial / content background: experience as a creator, editor, writer, or producer at a media brand, publisher, or creator-led company. you can write a hook and tell a story in 15 seconds. collectibles knowledge: working fluency in trading cards and collectibles, whether tcg (pokémon, magic, one piece, lorcana) or sports cards. you know what a chase card is, why grading matters, and what makes a pull go viral. trend awareness: you live on tiktok, youtube, x, and reddit, and know how to adapt a trend so it feels native to the brand rather than forced. technical skills: comfortable shooting on a phone and editing in capcut, premiere, or similar, and fluent in native platform analytics. communication skills: sharp writing and a consistent brand voice across every post. preferred skillsactive collector: you collect, break, or grade cards yourself and know the hobby's creators and communities. creator experience: you've built a following of your own on any platform. paid social exposure: experience feeding organic content into paid teams or working with ugc creators. app growth: experience driving installs for a mobile app. speed and volume: you ship a lot, learn fast, and keep quality high while doing it. adaptability: comfortable working in a fast-paced, remote environment with shifting priorities. company benefits:15 days of accrued pto7 days of sick-leave, front-loaded at the start of the year10 paid company holidaysgenerous vision, dental, and health benefits, with 97% contribution to premium401k matching

detail.desc: the foundationwe are the largest nonprofit fighting poverty, disease, and inequity around the world. founded on a simple premise: people everywhere, regardless of identity or circumstances, should have the chance to live healthy, productive lives. we believe our employees should reflect the rich diversity of the global populations we aim to serve. we provide an exceptional benefits package to employees and their families which include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with no premiums, generous paid time off, paid family leave, foundation-paid retirement contribution, regional holidays, and opportunities to engage in several employee communities. as a workplace, we’re committed to creating an environment for you to thrive both personally and professionally.the teamthe mission of the global policy & advocacy (gpa) division is to understand and shape the public policy debates affecting the foundation's work, build support for its major program and policy objectives, and develop partnerships and alliances that can advance the foundation's objectives nationally and globally. because the foundation's resources alone are not enough to solve the challenges ahead, gpa also supports advocacy efforts to engage diverse stakeholders and promote innovative solutions that advance our program goals. we work in close partnership with grantees, our colleagues in the global health, global development, global growth & opportunity, u.s. and gender equality programs and communications to build the environment in which all people can lead healthy and productive lives.the north america team (nat) is a team within gpa that develops and executes policy, advocacy, communications and government relations strategies to build political support and advance domestic and global programmatic priorities that are funded by, or executed within, the united states, canada, and the united nations.your rolethe senior officer, advocacy, international relations and policy planning (irpp), north america team, will be responsible for translating foundation strategies and priorities into policy-relevant arguments and advocacy opportunities across priority irpp markets, including canada and the un. the role will also lead special advocacy initiatives to advance maternal and child survival through sport and new partnerships, and related to global ai governance.working closely with the deputy director, canada and un leads, ai policy lead, and partnering with program, policy, communications, and other teams across the foundation, this role will support a collaborative, one foundation approach to market engagement. the successful candidate will bring strong political and institutional judgment, the ability to synthesize complex global health and development strategies, and experience connecting programmatic priorities to the political economy and institutional context of government and multilateral audiences.this is a 16 month limited term employment role. salary plus benefits are provided. relocation assistance and employer visa support are not available for this role. role can be located in seattle, wa or washington, dc.applications accepted until 5 pm pacific time on wednesday, november 18, 2026.must have unrestricted work authorization in the country where this position is located. the foundation does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. this includes direct company sponsorship and any work authorization requiring a written submission or other immigration support from the company (eg: h-1b, o-1, l-1, e, opt, stem-opt, cpt, tn, j-1, etc.).what you'll dospecial projects: lead special projects that test and strengthen new advocacy approaches to advance maternal and child survival, including:sports advocacy model: lead development of a strategic approach to better leverage sport to advance maternal and child survival. support the operationalization of new ideas and engagement models, connecting efforts and learning across irpp markets.global political coalition: lead an emerging initiative to build a new global political coalition in support of maternal and child survival through a new partnership. help shape the advocacy approach, develop relationships with new champions, and connect the initiative to foundation and market priorities.supporting emerging ai global governance advocacy partnershipspartner across the foundation: build effective working relationships with program, policy, communications, and other relevant teams to bring technical expertise and market insight together, align priorities, and coordinate contributions to shared work.understand foundation priorities: work with program and issue advocacy teams to understand the global development challenges the foundation seeks to address, the solutions set out in its strategies, and their intended impact, drawing on technical expertise across the foundation.assess market context: work with canada and un leads to assess the political economy, institutional mandates, priorities, capabilities, and constraints shaping each market, including canadian interests and the forward-looking agenda of the un ecosystem in new york.translate into market opportunities: bring these analyses together with market leads to identify how each market could advance foundation priorities and the expected impact of its contributions. develop market-specific policy proposals, arguments, and concrete asks with relevant foundation teams, supporting market leads in developing their advocacy approaches.support broader policy and development architecture work: partner with the deputy director on broader policy and development architecture questions, i.e. global cooperation trends, system reforms, etc., examining how global trends and institutional changes affect foundation priorities and the roles irpp markets can play.partner and contract management: engage and manage external partners and consultants supporting these workstreams. develop scopes of work, manage contracts, oversee deliverables and budgets, and coordinate with relevant internal teams to ensure work remains aligned with agreed objectives.your experience10+ years of experience in advocacy, government relations, public policy, multilateral engagement, or strategy, ideally in a nonprofit, governmental, philanthropic, or international setting. an advanced degree is a plus.demonstrated experience translating complex global health or development strategies into clear policy arguments, market-specific asks, and practical advocacy approaches, combining broad policy understanding with the ability to engage deeply with technical subjects.proven ability to craft big-picture strategic direction while developing and executing flexible, practical implementation plans.experience engaging external partners and managing contracts, including scopes of work, budgets, timelines, and deliverables.excellent verbal and written communication skills, with an ability to synthesize complex concepts, evidence, political context, and recommendations succinctly and persuasively.demonstrated ability to lead ambiguous or emerging workstreams, assess competing priorities, and deliver high-quality analysis and products for multiple internal collaborators.knowledge of global health, canada’s development policy and political ecosystem, and the un system would be an asset.highly collaborative, and low egomust have unrestricted work authorization in the country where this position is located. the foundation does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. this includes direct company sponsorship and any work authorization requiring a written submission or other immigration support from the company (eg: h-1b, o-1, l-1, e, opt, stem-opt, cpt, tn, j-1, etc.).the salary range for this role is $212,800 to $329,800 usd. we recognize high-wage market differences in seattle, wa and washington d.c., where our offices are located. the range for this role in these locations is $234,000 to $362,800 usd. as a mission-driven organization, we strive to balance competitive pay with our mission. new hires salaries are typically between the range minimum and the salary range midpoint. actual placement in the range will depend on a candidate’s job-related skills, experience, and expertise, as evaluated during the interview process.hiring requirementsas part of our standard hiring process for new employees, employment will be contingent upon successful completion of a background check.candidate accommodationswe’re committed to providing an inclusive and accessible hiring experience for all candidates. if you have a disability or medical condition and need an accommodation at any stage of the application or interview process—such as an asl interpreter, alternative interview format, or physical accessibility support—we’re happy to help. please contact hr@gatesfoundation.org with the position number and a brief description of your accommodation needs. requests will be handled confidentially.inclusion statementwe are dedicated to the belief that all lives have equal value. we strive for a global and cultural workplace that supports ever greater diversity, equity, and inclusion — of voices, ideas, and approaches — and we support this diversity through all our employment practices.all applicants and employees who are drawn to serve our mission will enjoy equality of opportunity and fair treatment without regard to race, color, age, religion, pregnancy, sex, sexual orientation, disability, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, and prior protected activity.

engagement, market access pull-through, and commercial execution within central precocious puberty (cpp).this is a hands-on, player-coach leadership role within a lean and agile rare disease business. the director is accountable for both developing strategy and personally driving execution of the highest-priority initiatives. success requires the ability to move seamlessly from executive-level planning to tactical implementation, performance analysis, field engagement, and problem solving.the director will lead a team of 2marketers while partnering closely with sales, medical affairs, market access, regulatory, legal, compliance, analytics, finance, supply chain, and sales training. the position requires a strong sense of ownership, urgency, accountability, and a demonstrated ability to translate customer insights into actions that improve business performance.essential duties & responsibilitiesbrand strategy & business leadership own the end-to-end u.s. brand strategy for fensolvi, including positioning, messaging, patient identification, customer engagement, access support, and lifecycle management. lead annual brand planning, long-range planning, forecasting assumptions, tactical planning, and budget recommendations. identify growth opportunities, business risks, market shifts, and competitive threats and translate findings into actionable business plans. own marketing's contribution to revenue growth, market share, patient starts, patient identification, and overall business performance. serve as a key member of the pediatric endocrinology leadership team and contribute to broader business strategy and decision making. commercial execution personally drive development and execution of priority marketing initiatives across hcp, caregiver, patient, digital, social, field, congress, and market access channels. translate strategy into clear deliverables, project plans, milestones, success measures, and execution priorities. maintain active involvement in campaign development, messaging, promotional materials, digital initiatives, field tools, and customer-facing programs. establish a disciplined operating cadence to evaluate business performance and rapidly adjust tactics based on results. lead commercialization efforts related to new data, publications, congress activity, competitive developments, and guideline updates. customer & market insights develop a deep understanding of the cpp patient journey, including patient identification, referral pathways, diagnosis, treatment selection, reimbursement, onboarding, and persistence. regularly engage with pediatric endocrinologists, key opinion leaders, caregivers, advocacy stakeholders, and field teams. conduct field travel, customer visits, advisory boards, and congress participation to maintain direct marketplace understanding. translate customer, market, competitive, and field insights into measurable actions that improve commercial effectiveness. market access & patient services partner closely with market access to support reimbursement, pull-through, hub, patient support, buy-and-bill, and access optimization initiatives. support commercial strategies that improve time-to-therapy, patient initiation, treatment persistence, and access expansion. evaluate payer trends, reimbursement barriers, medicaid opportunities, and competitive access changes to inform brand strategy. omnichannel & data-driven marketing lead omnichannel strategy and optimization across all customer segments. establish kpis and performance dashboards to monitor campaign effectiveness and return on investment. use analytics, customer insights, and performance data to continuously improve commercial execution. ensure marketing investments are focused on activities with the highest business impact. cross-functional leadership build strong partnerships across sales, medical affairs, market access, regulatory, legal, compliance, finance, analytics, and sales training. align stakeholders around key business priorities and remove barriers to execution. lead cross-functional brand teams and ensure coordinated delivery of critical initiatives. communicate brand strategy, performance updates, risks, and opportunities to senior leadership. agency & vendor management manage agency and vendor relationships, budgets, deliverables, timelines, and performance expectations. ensure agencies supplement internal capabilities rather than own critical strategic decisions. hold partners accountable for quality, innovation, speed, budget compliance, and business impact. team leadership lead, coach, and develop a three-person marketing team, including an assistant product manager and senior product manager. create a culture of accountability, ownership, collaboration, and continuous improvement. develop team capabilities while maintaining direct involvement in critical business decisions and high-priority initiatives. establish clear goals, development plans, performance expectations, and succession planning for all direct reports.  perform various other duties as assigned.leadership profile a player-coach: balances strategic leadership with hands-on execution and personally drives critical business initiatives.an owner: takes accountability for results, proactively identifies issues, and solves problems without waiting for direction.a doer: converts insights into action, drives decisions, and delivers outcomes in a practical and timely manner.commercially minded: understands the financial drivers of the business and prioritizes resources accordingly.customer connected: maintains firsthand understanding of customers, patients, caregivers, field teams, and market dynamics.agile & resourceful: thrives in ambiguity and delivers results within a lean organizational structure.highly collaborative: builds trust across functions and successfully aligns diverse stakeholders toward common goals.key performance indicators brand performance achieve or exceed approved annual revenue, demand, and market share objectives. deliver growth in patient starts, patient identification, and treatment persistence metrics. commercial execution execute at least 90% of priority brand initiatives on time and within approved budget. maintain execution excellence across promotional, educational, digital, and access-related initiatives. omnichannel effectiveness improve key engagement, conversion, and customer interaction metrics year over year. demonstrate measurable return on investment for major marketing investments. insight-to-action translate significant market, customer, competitive, and performance insights into documented action plans within established business-review timelines. field engagement maintain regular customer-facing engagement through field travel, advisory boards, conferences, and customer interactions. demonstrate direct marketplace insights that influence business decisions. budget management manage spending within approved budget parameters and maintain accurate forecasting. team development ensure direct reports have clear goals, development plans, and ongoing coaching. build organizational capability and succession readiness within the marketing team. compliance maintain adherence to all promotional review, compliance, legal, and regulatory detail.desc: hiring departmentmarketing & communicationsjob descriptionmissouri university of science and technology (missouri s&t) is looking for an exceptional communicator for the position of senior strategic communications consultant to work with leaders within our college of engineering and computing (cec) as part of a central communications, outreach and engagement team. this position requires talent, tact and tenacity, strong writing and storytelling skills, a collaborative mindset, the ability to influence others, political savvy, an enterprising outlook, and good doses of creativity, dauntless positivity in the face of difficulty, humor and humility.this position reports to the director of strategic communications in the marketing and communications department, with dotted-line reporting to either the vice provost and dean of the college or an associate dean of the college. the position works closely with other staff within communications, outreach and engagement to achieve the college’s strategic goals.goals and responsibilitiesresponsibilitiesthe person in this position will be responsible for collaboratively developing comprehensive college-level marketing and communications strategies in partnership with fellow marketing and communications staff and in collaboration with leaders, staff and faculty in the college. this will involve:developing effective external relations for the college in collaboration with the central marketing and communicationsadvising the vice provost and dean, associate deans, and department chairs on communications strategies and outreachcoordinating with development and alumni relations staff on alumni and donor relations communications and marketingdeveloping written content for marketing materials that support the college’s marketing and visibility goals, including print and digital communications materials, such as news releases, print and electronic newsletters, and website contentdeveloping content for and managing college-level social media channelsproviding expertise and assistance for other staff within the college and departments who are responsible for mid- to high-level communications tasks, such as online content, newsletters, etc.positioning the vice provost and dean, associate deans, department chairs and other college faculty as thought leaders and influencers to enhance the university’s visibility and influenceensuring consistent messaging, brand identity and achievement of marketing goals between the college and the university at largealong with the user interface and user experience designer (ux/ui designer), attending college-level meetings as co-liaison between the college and the marketing and communications departmentcoordinating with ux/ui designer on user experience with cec website and department websitestasks for cecnews and feature writing on behalf of cec, including press releases, cec and university website articles, with a heavy emphasis on writing about cec research.marketing materials for cec.u.s. news influencer marketing, including e-newsletter (6-8/year) and postcards of major announcements (new dean, etc.)cec social media posting (facebook, linkedin).cec internal communications (dean’s internal newsletter).strategic communications initiatives for the college.assist with departmental email newsletters (advise on content, edit copy, recommend stories, etc.)maintain contact and strong relations with cec leaders, including department chairs.coordinate requests for print and digital marketing materials related to cec and its academic departments. minimum qualificationsa bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 4 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessaryanticipated hiring rangethe anticipated hiring range for this position has been established as $60,944-$85,176 annually.salary is determined by a variety of factors, including but not limited to, the individual’s particular combination of education, skills, and experience, as well as organizational requirements.your total compensation goes beyond the number on your paycheck. the university of missouri provides generous leave, health plans, and retirement contributions that add to your bottom line.grade: ggs 11university title: senior strategic communications consultantto review the university of missouri’s staff compensation structure you can view the job code detail page. internal applicants can determine their university title by accessing the talent profile tile in myhr.application deadlineapplications will be accepted until this position is filled.sponsorship informationemployment visa sponsorship is not available for this position.community informationuniversity informationmissouri s&t is one of the nation's leading research universities with over 100-degree programs in 39 disciplines. it was founded in 1870 as one of the first technological institutions west of the mississippi river. located about 100 miles west of st. louis in the vibrant community of rolla, missouri s&t is an accessible, safe, and friendly campus surrounded by ozarks' scenery. missouri s&t offers undergraduate degrees in engineering, the sciences, liberal arts, humanities, and business, with m.s. and ph.d. programs available in many of the science and engineering programs. with over 7,000 students and 300 faculty, missouri s&t is big enough to accommodate a broad population, yet small enough for individuals to build high visibility and impactful careers.college of engineering & computing (cec)missouri s&t’s college of engineering and computing is the largest of three colleges at s&t, accounting for approximately 80% of the total enrollment (about 4,500 undergraduates and 800 graduate students). the college includes more than 170 ranked faculty members who serve in 16 undergraduate programs, all with master’s and doctoral equivalents organized into nine academic departments. the college recently added a bachelor’s degree in biomedical engineering and a ph.d. in bioengineering, both starting in fall 2024. missouri s&t, supported by the college of engineering and computing, is nationally recognized for its career outcomes and roi.about rollarolla, missouri offers several great advantages that help individuals enjoy a high quality of life. rolla is an ideal place for families, with its low cost of living, excellent schools, safe neighborhoods, and a range of recreational activities suitable for all ages. the ozark scenic riverways and beautiful landscapes offers abundant opportunities for outdoor enthusiasts of every lifestyle. with its vibrant community, rolla hosts multiple events, concerts, art exhibitions, and theater performances throughout the year. the university’s leach theatre showcases nationally renowned performers for campus and community alike. overall, living in rolla offers a high quality of life with a supportive community, affordable living, beautiful natural surroundings, and numerous opportunities for personal and professional growth.benefit eligibilitythis position is eligible for university benefits. as part of your total compensation, the university offers a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental and vision plans, retirement, paid time off, short- and long-term disability, paid parental leave, paid caregiver leave, and educational fee discounts for all four um system campuses. for additional information on university benefits, please visit the faculty & staff benefits website at https://www.umsystem.edu/departments-staff/human-resources/benefits-retirementequal employment opportunitythe university of missouri is an equal opportunity employer.to request ada accommodations, please call the office of equity & title ix at 573-341-7734.

detail.desc: about usgirl scouts of the usawe are girl scouts of the usa (gsusa), a nonprofit organization dedicated to building girls of courage, confidence, and character, who make the world a better place.from coast to coast and across the globe, gsusa provides programs built specifically for girls, meant to evolve alongside them as they discover who they are, explore their passions, and develop hands-on skills. backed by millions of alums and a network of dedicated adult volunteers and mentors, girl scouts of all backgrounds and abilities rise to meet new challenges, tap into the power inside them, and build the confidence to let it shine. they find their strengths in science labs and on hiking trails, at cookie booths and in front of city councils. along the way, they uncover the tools they need to lead with joy, on their own terms. and gsusa is there to support and inspire them every step of the way, working with 111 local councils across the country and usa girl scouts overseas to deliver our life-changing girl scout leadership experience.if you believe in the promise and potential of all girls and are inspired by girl scouts’ mission of building girls of courage, confidence, and character, who make the world a better place, we’d love to hear from you.corporate affairs helps care for and strengthen the girl scout brand by building trust, relevance, and meaningful connections with both internal and external audiences. through thoughtful, engaging storytelling, they elevate the “voice of the girl,” making sure her experiences, accomplishments, and impact are always front and center.the team delivers this work through a mix of internal and external communications, media relations, cultural assets, and government affairs, helping ensure clear, consistent, and compelling messages across every channel. by sharing the girl scout story in authentic and inspiring ways, the team helps audiences better understand who we are, what we stand for, and why our work matters. ultimately, the team’s goal is to make sure the girl scout brand remains trusted, relevant, and deeply connected to the girl scout mission everywhere our story is told. you will the associate, external communications is a resourceful, proactive storyteller who helps more people understand the experiences and impact of girl scouting. this role seeks out compelling stories with national potential and helps bring them to life through earned media.working as part of the external communications team, the associate listens closely, asks thoughtful questions, and connects ideas shared in internal meetings to broader cultural conversations and media opportunities. the role uncovers promising leads across gsusa and the girl scout movement, surfaces them to the team and its public relations agency partner, and develops them into timely, distinctive pitches and content that bring girl scouts’ brand platform, the power within, into public conversation across audiences and media.the associate also supports day-to-day media outreach; drafts and organizes press materials, briefing documents, and toolkits; tracks coverage and trends; helps prepare spokespeople; and contributes to storytelling around key moments, from the iconic girl scout cookie program to national research on the lives of girls.this is an opportunity for a communications professional who takes initiative, pursues promising opportunities, and turns complex information into compelling narratives. success requires curiosity, sound judgment, creativity, and the drive to collaborate across teams, spot connections others may miss, and strengthen girl scouts’ national presence.essential responsibilitiesthe associate, external communications supports gsusa's national earned media and storytelling work. most of the role's time is spent finding, developing, and placing stories.story development and media relations identify and source proactive story leads from across gsusa, the movement's 111 councils, national research, and the gsusa collection and juliette gordon low birthplace. surface the most promising ones to the team and agency partner with a recommended angle and target outlets.  identify timely hooks for girl scout stories, spokespeople, and research by mining news cycles and what’s trending.  draft press materials, including pitches, press releases, talking points, faqs, and briefing documents that reflect gsusa's key messages and the power within brand platform.  maintain media lists, the proactive media calendar, and the coverage tracker.  support thought leadership moments from planning through execution, including national research releases, speaking opportunities, events, and girl-centered activations.  prepare spokespeople for interviews with briefing documents, message points, and anticipated questions. coordinate interview logistics and staff media opportunities in person and virtually. agency and influencer collaboration serve as the day-to-day liaison with gsusa's public relations agency. this includes sharing briefs and story leads, tracking deliverables and timelines, and consolidating internal feedback.  support influencer and creator work in partnership with marketing and other teams by vetting talent for brand fit and values alignment, developing content and activation ideas, and finding ways to extend influencer work into earned storytelling.  maintain the earned influencer roster and relationship history. council support and sensitive issues  coordinate with council communications staff on national campaigns and key moments, including the girl scout cookie program.  monitor the media line and inbound inquiries. respond to routine questions and route others as directed.  support sensitive-issues monitoring by flagging emerging risks early. help draft holding statements and response materials under team direction. measurement and reporting  track and analyze coverage and earned influence performance against campaign and annual goals, including placements, reach, message pull-through, and share of voice.  prepare regular performance summaries, including inputs to quarterly organizational performance reporting. team operations keep external communications workstreams on schedule by tracking next steps, deliverables, and owners across teams.  coordinate the team's contracts with legal and procurement, and process invoices with finance.  maintain accurate timelines, files, and project documentation. schedule and availability**this is a full-time role. national news cycles, live events, and girl scout cookie season may occasionally require evening or weekend work.**note: this job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or activities required of the role. reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.required competenciesinitiative  resourceful self-starter who anticipates needs, follows through on commitments, and finds practical ways to move work forward. curiosity naturally curious and skilled at asking thoughtful questions, listening for possibilities, and connecting ideas across teams and conversations  passionate storyteller with excellent writing skills and the ability to adapt stories for print, broadcast, digital, social, and emerging media news judgement strong instinct for girl scout stories, people, research, and moments with national relevance, and for how to adapt them across print, broadcast, digital, social, and emerging media collaboration surfaces opportunities clearly, works effectively with colleagues, councils, and agency partners, and takes feedback well. cultural awareness attuned to news cycles, audience interests, social media, and cultural trends. judgment and discretion knows when to escalate, when to hold, and how to handle sensitive information. detail and accountability delivers accurate, timely work in a fast-moving environment. mission and brand stewardship understands and values the girl scout mission and the power within brand platform. required technical skills advanced proficiency in microsoft office, including excel for trackers and reporting and powerpoint for briefing materials.  proficiency in at least one media database or monitoring platform, such as cision, muck rack, or meltwater.  fluency with social and creator platforms, including instagram, tiktok, youtube, and linkedin, as sources of stories, trends, and talent.  practical use of microsoft copilot and other generative ai tools for research, drafting, and synthesis, with sound judgment about accuracy, sourcing, and confidentiality.  you need  bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience  minimum of 3 years’ experience in a corporate environment  demonstrated record of securing earned media placements with national or regional outlets through original pitching. candidates should be able to share examples of pitches and the coverage that resulted.  strong writing skills across press materials, including releases, pitches, media advisories, talking points, faqs, and briefing documents, with copy that is accurate, on message, and ready for review with minimal revision.  working knowledge of how newsrooms, broadcast bookers, and digital and creator media operate, including news cycles, embargoes, exclusives, and attribution.  experience tracking and reporting on coverage and earned influence performance (reach, impressions, message pull-through, share of voice) and turning results into clear, usable summaries.  working familiarity with influencer and creator partnerships, including vetting for brand fit and alignment and understanding disclosure requirements under the ftc endorsement guides.  experience working with or at a public relations agency, including managing briefs, timelines, and deliverables.  understanding of issues monitoring and rapid response, and demonstrated discretion with confidential and sensitive information.  experience coordinating multiple concurrent workstreams alongside routine administrative processes such as contracts, invoices, and vendor documentation, with consistent accuracy.  salary range:  $66,000 - $75,000this represents the present low and high end of the pay range for this position. this pay range is only applicable to nyc metro-based employees, on a hybrid schedule. actual pay will vary based on various factors, including but not limited to experience. what we offer: girl scouts is powered by people, and we encourage our team members to be their best selves in and out of the office. we place a high priority on flexibility and offer a competitive employee salary and benefits package that includes: paid time off:  gsusa offers 20+ days of paid time off, 2 floating holidays, as well as 9 workplace holidays per year. gsusa staff also enjoy a paid holiday year-end office closure between christmas and new year's. other benefits : medical and behavior al health coverageplan options with individual and family coverage which includes wellness, hospitalization, and fertility assistance .both plans with health savings accountscompany-paid life insuranceflexible work arrangements12 weeks of paid parental leave401(k) with company matchsick leaveshort- and long-term disability for salary continuationhealth and wellness classes and activities throughout the year physical demands:  the physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to average.position type / expected hours of work: this is a full-time position. days and hours of work are monday through friday with a 35 hour per week schedule. occasional evenings and weekends work wanted: a brand builder & spirited disruptor(or the more official title: brand manager, green river)location: louisville, ky / hybrid*hybrid candidates will need to be in kentucky a few times a month (fair warning: you may never want to leave). and some nights, weekends and travel come with the territory. tailgates don't run themselves, after all.who we are:green river has been distilling in owensboro, kentucky since 1885. while our bourbon was named “world’s best bourbon” at the 2025 new york world spirits competition, we still take pride in selling it at a fair price, without charging extra for the hype, the scarcity or all that velvet-rope nonsense. we call it “bourbon without the bullsh!t.”it’s not just a tagline. it’s how we think about bourbon, how we build the brand, and how we run the business, including how we hire. so here’s the job, described honestly.what’s the job:you’ll lead green river day-to-day with one pretty simple ambition: disrupt the whiskey category and build an american bourbon brand that people genuinely give a sh!t about.this is a hands-on position. you’ll write the plan, then make it happen. new bottle launches. big selling seasons. bar and store displays that earn their space. shooting real ads with real team members on a real lunch break (yes, we did that). and executing ideas that make people say, “wait, a bourbon brand did what now?”you’ll connect the dots across all our partners, while keeping an eye on what actually matters: who knows us, who’s buying us, what they care about, what’s working and what we should do next. you’ll own the budget and the scoreboard too, knowing where to put our money and when it’s time to take a big swing.and you’ll make sure the idea survives all the way to market, from the campaign brief to the sales meeting to the shelf, bar or tailgate where a real bourbon drinker actually sees it. just so you know, we’d much rather debate an idea that makes us uncomfortable than nod politely at a safe one.who you are:you’re a visionary brand builder with a maverick streak. you see where the category is going, where it’s stuck, and where green river has permission to go somewhere else. you have a point of view, you see opportunities other people miss, and you have the ideas and the ability to turn them into work that actually gets into market.you’re equally comfortable with the big idea and the work required to make it real. you can write the brief, build the plan, rally the room, challenge an agency, manage the details and connect creative, social, pr, activation, sales and our partners around a shared ambition.you know when to challenge convention, when to take a calculated risk and when an idea is worth fighting for. you bring people with you, but you don’t need consensus before having a point of view. you’re constantly looking for a better way to work, whether that means ai, new technology or simply refusing to do something the slow way because that’s how it’s always been done.above all, you want ownership. you want the freedom and responsibility to lead green river in disrupting the whiskey space, not just manage the next campaign. if who you are likes who we are, let’s grab a pour and chat. but you must be over 21 to enjoy the pour. (hr made us put this!)   full legal job description including physical requirements available upon request.
