google ventures and insight partners.it’s still day 0: now is the time to re-engineer how work gets done with ai at the core, and our toughest challenges still lie ahead. we’re looking for people seeking the hardest, most fulfilling work of their lives.how we workfour principles guide us:velocity. optimize for rate of learning. take action, get feedback, get better. hospitality. sweat the experience. delight customers, candidates and colleagues, even when it’s inconvenient. transparency. public unless private. share context openly within the company so people and agents can take initiative. end-to-end. deliver outcomes, not tasks. step beyond your job description and see the work through. the role:we’re looking for a brand designer to shape how metaview shows up in the world.you’ll work across every expression of our brand, from our website and product launches to campaigns, events, video, and everything in between. you’ll work closely with design, marketing, product, and our founders to turn complex products and ideas into work that feels simple, distinctive, and unmistakably metaview.we care deeply about craft, but also about how we produce it. we’re looking for someone who thinks in systems, gets close to the technology, and builds foundations that help us move faster without lowering the bar.what you'll do:website: maintain and evolve our public site, keeping it sharp, fresh, and differentiated. brand system: evolve metaview’s visual identity and turn it into scalable systems and toolkits across typography, color, illustration, icons, photography, and motion. campaigns & collateral: create standout work across digital, social, print, events, swag, and other brand moments, from concept through production. illustration & graphics: develop distinctive visuals for our website, product experiences, campaigns, and other channels. video: storyboard and direct the visual style of product explainers and brand videos. animation skills are a bonus, not a requirement. presentations: design compelling decks and assets that bring metaview’s story to life. collaboration: partner closely with marketing, product design, video, events, and operations from initial brief through final delivery. what you bring:a strong portfolio showing exceptional brand thinking, visual storytelling, typography, layout, and art direction across digital and physical touchpoints. excellent creative judgment: you can take an ambiguous brief, find the sharpest idea, and turn it into polished, distinctive work. high standards and high velocity: you care deeply about craft, sweat the details, and know when to move quickly. high agency and low ego: you take ownership, work autonomously, collaborate well, and stay hands-on from concept through production. a first-principles mindset and appetite for solving hard creative problems rather than defaulting to what’s been done before. genuine curiosity about ai and excitement to help define the visual language of a company building at the frontier. what we offer:high compensation, through cash and equity. we'll pay for any ai tools & books/resources you need as part of your role. unlimited pto. a ramp card for your wfh setup and the freedom to buy lunch & dinner any time you're in the office. the best co-workers you’ll ever have, in an environment that fosters cohesion, collaboration, and performance. supreme rate-of-learning as we re-orient how the world works with ai.

in 1954, eero saarinen designed a branch office with glass walls, no offices, and a completely open floor plan in columbus, indiana. it was surrounded by trees; the furniture was made by herman miller; the lobby flooring was thick, rustic brick. it was built with transparency and community at its core. since then, a lot of things have happened — saarinen's branch is now a conference center, people increasingly live on the internet, and it's hard to think of a single financial institution that still applies design thinking to their company.mercury is on a mission to defy those expectations. we're a financial technology company that helps startups spend less time banking* and more time building. we believe that the key to our success revolves around thoughtful design — and we hold the craft of that design to an exceptionally high standard. we're looking for a staff brand designer who sets that bar: someone whose eye is so precise, and whose execution is so considered, that the work around them gets better just by virtue of their presence.this is a role for a designer who sweats the details that most people don't notice — the type hierarchy, the negative space, the grid, the crop. someone who has developed a genuine aesthetic philosophy over years of doing hard work at a high level, and who brings that philosophy to everything they touch. you'll own the most technically complex brand design work at mercury, provide craft oversight across the brand studio, and help define what visual excellence looks like as our brand continues to evolve.mercury is a fintech company, not an fdic-insured bank. banking services provided through choice financial group and column n.a., members fdic.in this role, you’ll:set and uphold the craft standard for mercury's brand — across campaigns, web, social, events, and every surface the brand touches.lead the most technically complex and high-visibility brand design projects end-to-end, from brief through delivery.partner with a staff-level brand designer and creative leadership to co-lead the evolution of mercury's creative direction — defining and executing visual standards across typography, imagery, layout, and motion.provide hands-on craft oversight across brand studio output — reviewing work, raising the quality floor, and helping the team make better decisions.commission and art-direct external creatives: photographers, illustrators, and motion designers.develop brand system documentation and decision-making frameworks that help the team move with confidence and consistency.mentor ic3 and ic4 designers through critique, pairing, and direct feedback — elevating their craft through the work, not just in conversation.collaborate with brand strategists, copywriters, pmms, and leadership on how mercury shows up across all channels.shape how brand studio uses ai in its craft. you’ll set the standard for where ai belongs in the creative process, build ai-ready brand guidelines the team can design against, and hold the quality bar as these tools become part of how work gets made.what you’ll bring:a portfolio that is simply excellent — work that demonstrates mastery of typography, layout, color, and composition across a range of brand contexts.a clear and deeply held aesthetic point of view: you can articulate what makes something great and what makes something fall short, and you've built that perspective through years of rigorous practice.fluency in brand systems — you understand how to build for scale and consistency, and you've stewarded a brand through growth or change.7–10+ years of brand design experience, with a background that includes high-craft environments: agency, fashion, elevated consumer, or design-forward tech.experience operating at a staff level: you work autonomously, influence without authority, and make decisions that shape the output of an entire team.proficiency in figma and hands-on experience contributing to or owning a design system.strong verbal and presentation skills — you can communicate the process, intent, and impact of your design decisions with clarity.the judgment to know when to zoom in and when to zoom out, and the discipline to hold both at once.a considered point of view on ai’s place in high-craft design. you’ve used ai tooling in real creative work and can guide a team on where it belongs and how to use it without lowering the bar.curiosity, restraint, and a genuine passion for doing work that's worth doing.mercury values diversity & belonging and is proud to be an expertise, multi-format content production, and client communication.this is not a support role. you are a recognised authority in investments content strategy — someone who brings deep knowledge of senior levels of a large, global organisation. you follow the latest developments in your field closely and adapt them with speed and intelligence to the demands of the business.your remit spans the full breadth of citi wealth's investment product portfolio — from equities and fixed income to multi-asset strategies and alternative investments. you are not a specialist in one asset class or one the full range of materials required for communications aimed at healthcare professionals and consumers. the client portfolio spans human and animal health, and a wide range of therapy areas and detail.desc: the foundationwe are the largest nonprofit fighting poverty, disease, and inequity around the world. founded on a simple premise: people everywhere, regardless of identity or circumstances, should have the chance to live healthy, productive lives. we believe our employees should reflect the rich diversity of the global populations we aim to serve. we provide an exceptional benefits package to employees and their families which include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with no premiums, generous paid time off, paid family leave, foundation-paid retirement contribution, regional holidays, and opportunities to engage in several employee communities. as a workplace, we’re committed to creating an environment for you to thrive both personally and professionally.the teamthe mission of the global policy & advocacy (gpa) division is to understand and shape the public policy debates affecting the foundation's work, build support for its major program and policy objectives, and develop partnerships and alliances that can advance the foundation's objectives nationally and globally. because the foundation's resources alone are not enough to solve the challenges ahead, gpa also supports advocacy efforts to engage diverse collaborators and promote innovative solutions that advance our program goals. we work in close partnership with grantees, our colleagues in the global health, global development, global growth & opportunity, u.s. and gender equality programs and communications to build the environment in which all people have the opportunity to lead healthy and productive lives.requiredglobal program advocacy & communications (gpac) is the foundation’s global capability for issue advocacy and communications. gpac engages where work is cross-market, technically complex, and requires global assets and specialized expertise. working with our program, regional, and country teams, we help mobilize the financing, policy change, and public legitimacy required for impact. gpac’s core functions include: translating program priorities into advocacy strategies and asks: applying deep issue knowledge and policy expertise to translate technical program goals into actionable policy and financing priorities. developing and synthesizing evidence to influence decision-makers: investing in and translating research, data, and technical evidence into investment cases, policy content, and market-ready materials. building and mobilizing advocacy ecosystems: convening and aligning partners, coalitions, and champions to advance policy change, influence agendas, mobilize resources, and strengthen accountability. leading global issue communications: developing evidence-based narratives and communications assets; supporting strategic media engagement and campaigns; and anticipating and managing communications and reputational risks. providing specialized advocacy expertise: offering strategic counsel on complex advocacy challenges to build enabling policy, regulatory, and communications environments. facilitating cross-team collaboration and learning: connecting program, policy, communications, regional, and country teams; sharing intelligence on emerging risks and opportunities; and translating learnings across geographies.gpac partners with foundation colleagues and external stakeholders—including governments, multilateral institutions, civil society, philanthropy, the media, and others—to ensure that global strategies strengthen country-led advocacy and drive measurable progress.your rolethe global health sector is being redefined. development assistance for health has decreased significantly since its peak in 2021, major health multilaterals had difficulty meeting replenishment targets, and bilateral donors are shifting their funding approaches. at the same time, governments in africa and asia are raising domestic health spending and asserting leadership through the lusaka agenda, the accra reset, africa cdc, auda nepad, the african medicines agency, and india’s growing role as a source of vaccines, digital public infrastructure and ai for other countries. ai is moving from pilots into public health systems. the foundation has committed to spend its resources by 2045 to help ensure no mother, child or baby dies of a preventable cause, the next generation grows up in a world without deadly infectious diseases, and hundreds of millions of people break free from poverty.the director, global program advocacy and communications (global pac), health leads the foundation’s global health advocacy through this transition. the director provides strategic leadership for the team that turns the foundation’s health priorities into political will, financing and policy change, and helps build a system of health financing and policy that countries own and that will last beyond any single donor, including the foundation.the director leads global pac health, including the program partner teams aligned to the global health, global development and gender equality divisions, and health communications. the team’s centralized capabilities drive global outcomes and create the narratives, global public goods, evidence, and specialized policy capacity that make market- and country-led advocacy more effective. this includes building investment cases with program and finance and resource mobilization teams, building partner coalitions, crafting issue narratives and spotting risks, and strengthening the policy and regulatory environments needed to advance our health financing and policy goals. the team’s work supports the foundation’s goals and the gpa division priorities that advance them: maternal & child survival, health research and development (r&d), innovation introduction, and health financing.the director works across the foundation with the program strategy teams (psts) and division leadership teams, and across gpa with the market-led teams in europe, middle east and east asia (emeea), north america (nat), africa, india and south/southeast asia, the development policy and finance (dpaf) team, and the philanthropic partnership team (ppt), so that foundation priorities reach decision-makers through strategic, coordinated advocacy. the director leads the team that serves as gpa’s front door to the psts and division leadership and aligns gpa’s advocacy capabilities behind the foundation’s highest-impact priorities.global and country teams each hold something the other needs. seattle sits close to psts, government relations teams in donor capital are close to financing decisions, and regional and country teams hold the context, and the relationship with governments in our delivery geographies the director makes the partnership model between global and regional/country teams work: co-designing strategy with africa and india colleagues from the outset, sharing intelligence in both directions, advocating inside the foundation for country priorities with psts and division leaders, and leading gpac health on the connections and priorities a global team is best placed to do.the ideal leader understands and translates complex pst strategies and brings the best of gpa to them: its relationships, intelligence, financing expertise and communications capability. they have deep advocacy experience, strong knowledge of financing sources across bilateral, multilateral and philanthropic funders and the ability to work with the resource mobilization (rm) hub and other gpa teams to maximize resource mobilization. they understand how health systems are financed and run, how ministries of finance and health make budget decisions, and how to effect policy change at global, regional and national levels. they have earned credibility with leaders in governments and institutions across the global south. they are both a practitioner and an orchestrator: credible enough to speak in specifics on advocacy tactics, strategy and partners, and skilled at keeping many complex, interdependent efforts moving at once. they are decisive, with the credibility to define clearly what is and is not achievable and to bring colleagues with them. this role suits a leader who has worked in multiple parts of global health, in or with government, in multilateral, academic or research institutions, in civil society, or in industry.this role partners with the director, global pac global growth and opportunity (ggo) to co-lead the overall global pac team and reports to the president, gpa.applications accepted until friday, november 27th. locations considered for this role are seattle, wa, washington, dc and london, uk. as a global search for the best talent, all qualified senior leaders are encouraged to apply.what you'll dostrategy and leadershipset and implement the global pac health strategy. define where global pac health engages focusing on cross-market, technically complex or politically sensitive work and on reusable global assets that regional and country teams draw on. own the quality of the strategy and the delivery of its outcomes.lead through the gpa division priorities. own global pac health’s contribution to the division priorities on maternal & child survival, health r&d, innovation introduction and health financing, turning each priority into an integrated plan that links advocacy, financing, policy and communications. work with the relevant psts, regional and country advocacy teams, and gpa colleagues to set one clear strategy and ask for each priority, align the partners, coalitions and donors needed to deliver it, and use key global moments to build political commitment and mobilize resources. hold the team accountable for measurable progress, and make sure global efforts reinforce the work of country and regional teams.be a strategic partner to psts and serve as a bridge to gpa teams. develop a deep understanding of each pst’s strategy and lead the program partner leaders who represent gpa on pst and division leadership teams. bring the best of gpa to program teams in a coordinated way, translating technical priorities into clear policy and financing asks, meeting each team where it is while holding the line on what advocacy can and cannot achieve. bring regional and country perspectives into pst strategy early, before asks are set. bring hands-on advocacy expertise to sharpen the team’s engagement and strengthen the credibility of gpa’s counsel.partnership with regional and country teamsbuild one strategy with africa and india. co-design advocacy strategies, asks, and plans with the africa policy, government relations and partnerships (pgrp) and india pac teams from the start. clarify roles between gpac, regional and country teams in africa and india, and government relationships teams in donor markets. share intelligence in both directions and hold joint accountability for results.carry country evidence and leadership into global decisions. provide space in global platforms for analysis and champions from the regional/country efforts, including through replenishments and global moments such as the g20, the un general assembly and the world health assembly.broker south-south exchange. work with the india and africa teams to spread proven approaches across countries, including, ai tools, regulatory reform, local manufacturing when economically viable, and to support the growing role of india and african countries as suppliers of health innovation to other low- and middle-income countries.financing, architecture and ecosystemsdrive policy and financing alignment for health pst priorities. define the policy and financing asks for pst issues and lead pac’s contribution to replenishments, pledging moments and deal teams, coordinating advocacy, strengthening positioning and aligning partners and communications. work within the gpa resource mobilization (rm) hub model: partner with the gpa teams who lead funder relationships, opportunity development and deal brokerage, and with the rm hub on shared visibility of financing needs and sources, deal ownership and escalation.advocate for financing countries own health systems. with dpaf, the rm hub and regional teams, support the shift from aid dependence toward domestic resource mobilization, stronger budget execution, and blended and innovative finance. engage multilateral development banks and newer sources of finance, including gulf and asian governments and domestic and diaspora philanthropy.help shape the reform of global health architecture. help the foundation take clear, constructive positions as global health initiatives, un agencies and donors reorganize, consistent with the lusaka agenda and country-led platforms. promote one national plan, one budget and one accountability framework in each country. engage bilateral donors as they move to compact-based models so new agreements reinforce national systems.shape the global health advocacy ecosystem and build coalitions. steward a focused portfolio of health advocacy partners, guide pac’s engagement with disease-specific institutions and communities, and maintain accountability for results. convene multilateral institutions, civil society and philanthropic partners around shared goals, and build the investment cases, convenings and cross-market learning that make country and regional advocacy more effective.lead advocacy and partnerships on ai for health. with psts, the africa and india teams and gpa colleagues, advance the policy, financing and governance needed to move proven ai tools from pilots into government-owned health systems: lower costs and clear procurement pathways, the data and compute foundations low- and middle-income countries need, and standards for safety, equity and evidence. use ai to make gpac’s own advocacy and communications faster and better informed.issue communicationslead issue communications. oversee health communications, developing evidence-based narratives and communication assets, supporting strategic media engagement and campaigns, and in partnership with the communications division and regional teams, manage communications and reputational risks associated with the issue portfolio. make the case for health as an investment in growth. with the ggo team, show how health, nutrition and human capital drive productivity, jobs and economic growth, in terms finance ministers and investors use.co-leading global pacpartner with the director, global pac ggo to set shared direction, operating model and standards for global pac, align budget and portfolio decisions, and co-lead portfolio and strategy reviews.drive innovation and learning in advocacy. pilot new advocacy approaches, narratives and engagement models, measure results, including value for money and the defense of past gains, document what works and what does not, and share learning across pac and gpa to build pac as a center of excellence.people leadershiplead and develop the team. set a clear vision and a high bar for performance. lead, coach and grow leaders and individual contributors across time zones and geographies. hire and onboard talent, set clear expectations, give and seek feedback, support development, and hold people accountable. build an inclusive, energized team culture and lead people with care and clarity through organizational change.your experiencea master’s degree or equivalent demonstrated experience, preferably in public policy, public health, health economics, international relations or international development.15+ years of progressive, senior-level experience leading and developing senior teams and leading policy, advocacy and financing initiatives in global health and global development, or equivalent, preferably across government, multilateral, academic, non-profit and private sectors.experience working in or with governments in low- and middle-income countries, ideally in africa or south asia, and with multilateral agencies, development banks and global health institutions.professional or lived experience of health systems in low- and middle-income countries, and credibility with leaders of governments and institutions in the global south.deep knowledge of health financing and health systems: how budgets are set, released and spent, how domestic resource mobilization works, and how global health initiatives finance and deliver programs.demonstrated record of mobilizing resources across bilateral, multilateral, development bank and philanthropic funders, ideally in global health.mastery-level expertise in advocacy and influencing related to resource mobilization, policy analysis, communications, coalition building, and partnership development with diverse constituencies, including the private sector, policymakers, civil society, academia, multilateral agencies and development banks. campaign or strategic communications experience is an asset.proven ability to turn data, economic analysis and implementation evidence into investment cases and policy proposals decision-makers act on.hands-on advocacy credibility: able to speak in specifics on advocacy tactics, strategy and partners, and to steer multiple complex, interdependent workstreams at once while keeping command of the detail.strategy development and execution, including impact measurement, portfolio management and prioritization in a changing resource environment.working knowledge of digital public infrastructure, data and ai, and the policy, financing and governance questions they raise for health systems.ability to learn technical health subject matter quickly, earn the respect of psts and technical and program experts, and navigate complex, politically sensitive environments.excellent written and oral communication skills, and the ability to translate technical program strategy into clear, compelling asks for different audiences and cultures. professional working proficiency in french or portuguese is an asset.proven ability to build trusted relationships and drive outcomes inside a complex, matrixed organization: someone who defines clearly what can and cannot be achieved, and challenges senior colleagues constructively while preserving the partnership.excellent leadership, judgment, intellectual curiosity and diplomacy, with the ability to hold the line while meeting partners where they are, to lead through influence, and to build, lead and develop high-performing, inclusive teams, including through moments of change.willingness to travel a minimum of 30%, much of it in africa and asia.the salary range for this role is $299,100 to $463,500 usd. we recognize high-wage market differences in seattle, wa and washington d.c., where our offices are located. the range for this role in these locations is $328,900 to $509,900 usd. as a mission-driven organization, we strive to balance competitive pay with our mission. new hires salaries are typically between the range minimum and the salary range midpoint. actual placement in the range will depend on a candidate’s job-related skills, experience, and expertise, as evaluated during the interview process.hiring requirementsas part of our standard hiring process for new employees, employment will be contingent upon successful completion of a background check.candidate accommodationswe’re committed to providing an inclusive and accessible hiring experience for descriptionamazon’s last-mile delivery network touches millions of customers every day — and with that scale comes real scrutiny. legislation, regulatory shifts, and coordinated advocacy campaigns can move fast, and the stories they generate don’t wait for anyone. this role puts you at the center of how amazon identifies, understands, and responds to the issues that matter most to its last-mile delivery operations.as communications manager, last-mile issues and campaigns, you'll own the communications strategy for a portfolio that touches aspects of amazon's last-mile delivery model. last-mile delivery touches regulation, safety, and public trust, and this role sits at the center of how we communicate across all of it. you'll lead strategic narrative development and scenario planning that keeps the team ahead of legislative shifts, emerging campaigns, and related issues. you'll coordinate across relevant business lines and communications teams, partnering with policy comms, field comms, and others, to bring the right expertise to bear at the right moment and ensure amazon speaks with one clear, strategic voice. you'll draft the statements, talking points, and briefing documents that represent amazon externally, and you'll manage the feedback and approval cycles that come with them. you'll spend as much time seeding stories and shaping narratives as you do managing the reactive moments that come with the portfolio.you're a high-judgment communicator who doesn't flinch when things get complicated. you can hold multiple fast-moving situations at once without losing your footing, but what sets you apart is your ability to spot the issue before it breaks and start building the strategy, not just the response. you think clearly under pressure, write precisely on deadline, and know how to bring the right people together at the right moment. you're comfortable as an on-the-record spokesperson, and you know how to work with reporters to shape a story before it spirals. you think like a strategist, connecting dots across policy, operations, and reputation to protect and advance the business. you don't wait to be told there's a problem. you've already mapped the landscape, built the plan, and brought the right people to the table.this is a strong independent contributor role that reports into the core operations communications team within the global operations and workplace reputation team.key job responsibilitiesmanage complex, fast-moving, and unexpected communications challenges with high judgment and professionalism.be precise under tight deadlines and prioritize and manage multiple situations simultaneously.effectively represent amazon as an on-the-record spokesperson.work with reporters to correct and clarify breaking news stories.write, develop, and manage approvals of external communications materials dealing with sensitive and timely topics.participate in multi-stakeholder emergency response meetings to provide insight and guidance from an external communications point-of-view.a day in the lifeyou might start your morning scanning media coverage and legislative trackers to flag any new developments that could affect amazon’s last-mile operations — then pull together a quick brief for a leader heading into a sensitive meeting. by midday, you could be on a call with legal and public policy partners to assess the communications implications of a pending bill or regulatory action, working through the messaging framework and drafting an initial statement. in the afternoon, you may shift to handling a reactive media inquiry on a breaking story, coordinating approvals in real time while staying in close contact with the reporter to manage the narrative. you’ll close out by updating scenario plans for upcoming legislative milestones and checking in with issues managers across the team to make sure nothing’s falling through the cracks.about the teamwe’re a team of strategic communicators responsible for telling the story of how amazon gets people their packages — from the first mile to the last. we work across organizational boundaries to develop integrated communications strategies that inform, engage, and build trust with the audiences that matter most. we use data to shape our decisions, and we anticipate and mitigate reputational headwinds through cross-channel efforts. we value thoughtful collaboration, creative problem-solving, and a commitment to getting the details right.on the issues side of the team, we move fast and we move together. when a legislative campaign or regulatory challenge emerges, we’re the ones coordinating the response — aligning messaging across legal, policy, and business partners and making sure amazon’s voice is clear, consistent, and credible. we’re building for the long term — investing in mechanisms, relationships, and talent that will scale as amazon grows. if you want to do meaningful work alongside colleagues who care deeply about their craft and support each other’s growth, this is the team for you.basic qualifications bachelor's degree 7+ years of recent professional communications or public relations experiencepreferred qualifications experience in verbal and written communication for executive level leaders experience driving direction and alignment with cross-functional teamsamazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.our inclusive culture empowers amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. if you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. if the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your recruiting partner.the for supplemental life plans, eap, mental health support, medical advice line, flexible spending accounts, adoption and surrogacy reimbursement coverage), 401(k) matching, paid time off, and parental detail.desc: descriptiongo-to-market lead, category marketing this role is responsible for developing and leading the category marketing strategy for an assigned f2 business area, including fashion, sports & outdoors, or licensed sports. serving as the single-threaded marketing partner to category leadership, this leader translates business priorities, customer insights, assortment strategies, and commercial goals into annual and seasonal go-to-market plans that drive traffic, engagement, and growth.the go-to-market lead owns the category's integrated marketing roadmap, including campaign calendaring, investment prioritization, tier b targeted activations, tier c foundational programs, and category contributions to tier a tentpole moments. they develop a clear point of view on where marketing can most effectively support category growth, align cross-functional teams around prioritized customer moments, and ensure plans are grounded in measurable category objectives.this role partners closely with business, creative, product, bi, and traffic & targeting teams. the go-to-market lead provides the category inputs required to inform nasm and channel planning, including assortment priorities, deal calendars, customer audiences, launch milestones, and business goals.key job responsibilitiescategory marketing strategy & planning develop the annual and quarterly marketing strategy for an assigned category, translating business goals into clear customer, campaign, and investment priorities. establish the category's marketing narrative, strategic pillars, target audiences, and role within the broader f2 integrated marketing portfolio. identify the customer missions, seasonal shifts, cultural moments, launches, and category-specific opportunities where marketing can generate incremental business impact. build integrated plans that connect category priorities across campaigns, customer experiences, content, creative, and traffic-driving channels. identify emerging category trends, customer shifts, and growth opportunities that inform marketing strategy and investment recommendations.gtm ownership & campaign prioritization own the category's annual and seasonal gtm calendar, balancing business priorities, customer relevance, operational readiness, and available marketing capacity. lead tier b targeted and tier c foundational gtm activations from initial business intake through strategy, executional alignment, launch, and performance review. represent the category's priorities and customer needs within tier a tentpole planning, including major shopping events, seasonal campaigns, and cross-f2 initiatives. develop clear gtm briefs that define the customer problem, business opportunity, audience, value proposition, success metrics, dependencies, and activation approach. establish prioritization recommendations when category requests exceed available marketing, creative, or channel capacity. ensure campaigns have clear launch criteria, accountable owners, measurable objectives, and documented decisions.category partnership & business leadership serve as the primary marketing partner to category leadership and maintain a comprehensive understanding of the category's financial goals, assortment strategy, deal calendar, customer dynamics, and operational roadmap. translate category inputs into actionable marketing recommendations rather than functioning solely as an intake or execution partner. partner with category leaders to identify where marketing can meaningfully accelerate growth and flag areas where business, selection, pricing, or operational readiness may impact campaign effectiveness. lead annual and quarterly planning discussions that align category stakeholders around the highest-impact marketing priorities. provide category leadership and directors with visibility into upcoming campaigns, investment recommendations, dependencies, risks, and expected outcomes.cross-functional gtm leadership partner with creative and stores teams to ensure customer experiences and traffic-driving assets reflect a consistent category strategy and value proposition. work with product and technology teams to identify customer experience requirements, launch dependencies, merchandising needs, automation opportunities, and readiness risks. partner with finance and category teams to recommend category marketing budget allocation across campaigns, programs, and customer moments. provide the traffic & targeting lead with category goals, priority audiences, assortment inputs, deal details, timing, and campaign requirements to inform channel and nasm planning. partner with bi and channel teams to define measurement plans and interpret performance across campaigns and customer touchpoints. drive timely decisions, escalate unresolved dependencies, and maintain alignment across teams throughout the gtm lifecycle.performance management & leadership narratives own category-level marketing performance reporting, including campaign results, customer insights, business impact, lessons learned, and recommended actions. develop the marketing sections of category mbr and qbr narratives for senior leadership. connect individual campaign results to broader category trends, strategic priorities, and investment decisions. establish repeatable mechanisms for tracking category plans, launch health, marketing contribution, and progress against annual goals. use performance insights to refine future campaign strategy, audience priorities, activation criteria, and budget allocation.a day in the life meet with category leadership to review business performance, assortment priorities, upcoming launches, and areas where marketing support could accelerate growth. translate annual or seasonal business goals into an integrated gtm strategy and prioritized category marketing calendar. lead a cross-functional campaign working session to align product, stores, creative, traffic & targeting, and analytics partners on launch readiness and success metrics. review a proposed category activation and determine whether it has a clear customer insight, differentiated value proposition, sufficient selection, and measurable business opportunity. provide the traffic & targeting lead with category inputs for nasm and channel planning while maintaining accountability for the overall category strategy. develop an mbr or qbr narrative that explains performance, identifies key drivers and headwinds, and recommends actions for the next planning period. advise senior leaders on campaign prioritization, investment tradeoffs, launch risks, and the category’s forward-looking marketing roadmap.about the teamabout the teamf2 integrated marketing (f2m) owns the go-to-market process for time-bound, business-backed moments across fashion, sports & outdoors, premium, licensed sports, and luxury. we translate business priorities into customer-facing marketing activations that drive traffic, conversion, and engagement across shopping events, holidays, cultural moments, sports and entertainment, launches, and mission-based customer needs.the category gtm team serves as the strategic marketing interface to each f2 business. we develop category-level marketing strategies, establish annual and seasonal priorities, lead targeted and foundational gtm programs, and ensure category goals are represented within larger f2 tentpole moments. we work in close partnership with traffic & targeting, creative, stores, product, analytics, finance, and central marketing teams to turn business opportunities into cohesive and measurable customer activations.basic qualifications 6+ years of professional non-internship marketing experience detailsabout salesforcesalesforce is the #1 ai crm, where humans with agents drive customer success together. here, ambition meets action. tech meets trust. and innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. the world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through ai, driving innovation, and keeping salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? you’re in the right place! agentforce is the future of ai, and you are the future of salesforce.what you'll be doing & why it matterssalesforce's global ethics & integrity (ge&i) team is looking for a proactive, detail-oriented training and communications manager to join the compliance programs team. this is an individual contributor role. you will set the strategy for training and communications on ethics, integrity, and compliance matters, and own execution from start to finish. your work will give salesforce employees the information they need to prevent and reduce compliance risk.you'll be a key member of the salesforce legal team, which makes sure we do business to the highest legal and ethical standards. we want someone with experience in communications and learning for adult audiences who looks for ways to improve our program, especially through ai-driven solutions.core responsibilities & scopewith oversight from the director, compliance programs - global ethics & integrity:training and learningplan, build, and run the global compliance training plan, including the annual code of conduct training and targeted, risk-based courses. manage each course from design through rollout and ongoing maintenance.apply modern instructional design, such as micro-learning, scenario-based content, and ai-assisted development to improve engagement and retention.collaborate with cross-functional partners to improve the learning platforms, and support training assignment logic, localization, and completion tracking.track completion, engagement, and post-training effectiveness, and use the data to improve content and close knowledge gaps.communications and culturebuild and run an annual communications calendar including campaigns, awareness moments, toolkits, and leader and manager messaging on ethics, integrity, and compliance topics.turn complex legal and ethics & compliance concepts into clear, engaging guidance for global audiences, in writing, in presentations, and visually.ensure training and communications address emerging risks, policy changes, and trends from the data (internal and external).operations and external assessmentsmanage salesforce's responses to external ethics and compliance assessments, including ethisphere's world's most ethical companies, including gathering input and coordinating reviewers, and drafting and submission.use ai platforms, data tools, and automation to streamline how work gets done.test and roll out improvements to compliance processes, and set the standard for responsible ai use in training and communications.report insights and findings to leadership, clearly and concisely.support the ge&i team in handling employee questions and escalate them as needed.minimum requirements5+ years of experience in ethics and compliance, learning and development, or corporate communications, including direct experience managing training and communications on ethics, integrity, or compliance topics.bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.strong written, verbal, and visual communication skills, with the ability to adapt for varied audiences.proven ability to manage several stakeholders and competing priorities independently and on tight deadlines.experience with global programs and localization, and with cross-functional teams across time zones.hands-on experience using ai tools (such as generative ai assistants, ai-assisted content creation, or workflow automation) to produce content, analyze data, or streamline work.strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and comfort with metrics and reporting.preferred qualificationscompliance certification, such as ccep.familiarity with anti-corruption laws and compliance frameworks (fcpa, uk bribery act).experience with instructional design, multimedia production, or lms administration.experience building ai-enabled learning, such as simulations, scenario generation, or personalized learning paths.experience with salesforce, tableau, slack, or similar tools.experience preparing external ethics and compliance assessments or benchmarks.unleash your potentialwhen you join salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best, and our ai agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best. together, we’ll bring the power of agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for ai, and the world.accommodationsif you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please submit a request via this accommodations request form.please note that salesforce uses artificial intelligence (ai) tools to help our recruiters assess and evaluate candidates’ resumes and qualifications throughout the recruiting process. humans will always make any candidate selection and hiring decisions. please see our candidate privacy statement for more information about how we use your personal data and your rights, including with regard to use of ai tools and opt out options.posting statementsalesforce is an equal opportunity employer and maintains a policy of non-discrimination with all employees and applicants for employment. what does that mean exactly? it means that at salesforce, we believe in equality for all. and we believe we can lead the path to equality in part by creating a workplace that’s inclusive, and free from discrimination. know your rights: workplace discrimination is illegal. any employee or potential employee will be assessed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications – without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender expression or identity, transgender status, age, disability, veteran or marital status, political viewpoint, or other classifications protected by law. this policy applies to current and prospective employees, no matter where they are in their salesforce employment journey. it also applies to recruiting, hiring, job assignment, compensation, promotion, benefits, training, assessment of job performance, discipline, termination, and everything in between. recruiting, hiring, and promotion decisions at salesforce are fair and based on merit. the same goes for compensation, benefits, promotions, transfers, reduction in workforce, recall, training, and education.in the united states, compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, job level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. certain roles may be eligible for incentive compensation, equity, and benefits. salesforce offers a variety of benefits to help you live well including: time off programs, medical, dental, vision, mental health support, paid parental leave, life and disability insurance, 401(k), and an employee stock purchasing program. more details about company benefits can be found at the following link: https://www.salesforcebenefits.com.at salesforce, we believe in equitable compensation practices that reflect the dynamic nature of labor markets across various regions. the typical base salary range for this position is $117,400 - $177,600 annually. the range represents base salary only, and does not include company bonus, incentive for sales roles, equity or benefits, as applicable.

about covistacovista (nyse: cvsa) is america's largest healthcare educator, serving 100,000 students and supported by a community of 400,000 alumni across five accredited institutions. through personalized, tech-enabled education powered by 10,000 faculty and colleagues, covista expands access to healthcare careers and addresses the u.s. healthcare workforce shortage at scale. covista is the parent company of american university of the caribbean school of medicine, chamberlain university, ross university school of medicine, ross university school of veterinary medicine and walden university.our colleagues come from a wide range of backgrounds, business, academia, healthcare, government and nonprofits, and are part of a culture where doing exceptional work and making a meaningful difference for students and society aren't separate goals—they're one and the same. this means creating an environment where colleagues can develop new skills, build careers that match their ambitions and see the tangible impact of their work on healthcare education and workforce development. colleagues who deliver results and embrace new tools to work smarter are valued for their contributions. but what makes working at covista distinctive is our impact. our faculty and colleagues don't just support healthcare education—they shape it. this isn't abstract purpose work. it's solving real problems for real people in real communities while advancing careers.we operate on a hybrid schedule with four in-office days per week (monday–thursday). this approach enhances creativity, innovation, communication, and relationship-building, fostering a dynamic and collaborative work environment.for more information, visit covista.com and follow us on linkedin, instagram and youtube.job descriptionthis is a fast-paced and exciting role where you will help shape how the leader of america’s largest healthcare educator shows up, both inside the company and beyond it, at a moment when our story is growing in relevance and scope. as part of his communications team, you’ll be a strategic partner to a ceo who has a voice that’s unmistakably his own. you'll help decide where, when and how to use that voice to move the business forward. you’ll bring business savvy and a fresh pulse on what’s moving across content, the media landscape and culture, including healthcare and education, to sharpen ideas, spot the right moments and match each message to the channel, audience and stage where it will have the most impact. you’ll be part counselor, part editor and part strategist. the work is high-visibility and high-trust. you’ll partner closely with the executive office and senior leadership. you’ll also work across corporate affairs (investor relations, government and public affairs, alumni engagement and social impact) and with our institutions so that every appearance, post and message builds a clear, credible leadership presence that carries our purpose further.responsibilities:ceo voice and platform strategy help build and steward the ceo’s communications platform, including core narratives, signature themes and proof points that line up with covista’s business strategy and reputation goals elevate his authority by spotting the ideas, data and moments where covista can shape the national conversation on healthcare and education, and finding the formats that carry them furthest stay at the leading edge of how executives break through: track what’s working across media, platforms and formats and bring the ideas worth trying be a trusted editorial partner: a second set of eyes and a collaborator, keeping covista’s narrative consistent across every format and audience offer counsel on which moments to lead, which to amplify and which to skip, based on business priorities, news cycles and audience insight \channels, events and moments help plan the ceo’s external visibility across speaking engagements, conferences, media, industry forums, policy settings and executive social, choosing opportunities for business impact rather than volume connect the ceo’s voice to key business moments, including earnings, investor events, partnerships, research launches and major company milestones, working closely with investor relations and corporate communications help shape the ceo’s internal communications presence, including town halls, leadership forums and colleague messages, so his voice reaches our people as clearly as it reaches external audiences counsel, preparation and execution lead preparation for high-stakes moments, including briefing materials, messaging, q&a and rehearsal for media interviews, keynotes, panels and investor-facing settings draft and edit when needed, including speeches, remarks, bylines and presentations, while also editing and elevating the ceo’s own writing build and run the ceo’s communications calendar and operating rhythm with his chief of staff and executive assistant, making sure approvals, timelines and details are handled define and report on success measures for the ceo’s platform, connecting visibility and engagement to reputation and business outcomes use ai and technology to work smarter, sharpen insight and move faster  who thrives here: you’re a strategic communicator first. you know that the most valuable thing you can do for a ceo is help them say the right thing in the right place at the right moment, not write every word. you’re a trend spotter by instinct, seeing what’s breaking through in media, culture and executive communications before it’s obvious and turning it into thought leadership worth acting on. you’ve earned the trust of top executives by being candid, discreet and consistently right on judgment, so you’re confident pushing back and comfortable in any room with senior leaders. you have a great ear for voice, so the work gets stronger and still sounds like him. you’re energized by building rather than maintaining, drawn to a mission bigger than any single message and at your best as part of a team. qualificationsbachelor's degree in communications, marketing, journalism or a related field required. 10+ years of communications experience, including significant time advising a ceo or c-suite leader directly, whether in-house, at an agency or both strategic judgment: a track record of building an executive’s platform and choosing the channels, moments and opportunities that advanced business goals an exceptional editor’s ear: the ability to absorb a leader’s voice, sharpen their thinking and elevate their own writing across formats executive social expertise: hands-on experience shaping a senior leader’s linkedin presence with measurable impact business fluency: comfort working at the intersection of corporate reputation, investor relations and company strategy, ideally at a publicly traded company discretion and presence: trusted with sensitive information, steady in high-stakes situations, and confident counseling senior leaders comfort with ai tools: you actively use ai to produce better work, faster  preferred background: experience supporting executives at publicly traded companies is a plus, as is a background in higher education, healthcare or regulated industries. you move easily between strategic counsel and flawless execution. you build trust quickly with the executive office, internal partners and external stakeholders alike. a bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, marketing or a related field is required. if you want your best work to serve a mission this big, we’d like to meet you. additional informationin support of the pay transparency laws enacted across the country, the expected salary range for this position is between $100171.61 and $181034.70. actual pay will be adjusted based on job-related factors permitted by law, such as experience and training; geographic location; licensure and certifications; market factors; departmental budgets; and responsibility. our talent acquisition team will be happy to answer any questions you may have, and we look forward to learning more about your salary requirements. experiences that resonate with audiences and achieve business objectives.we are looking for dreamers and doers who have the passion to champion big ideas and the talent to bring them to life. a place of acceptance and open dialogue, we strive to foster a culture where differences are not just valued, but celebrated. come do your best and be your best in a casual yet vibrant workplace where we company overviewat motorola solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. we’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. we build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.department overviewat motorola solutions, we build technologies that help people be their best in the moments that matter. our products support people working in complex, high-stakes environments — from public safety and emergency communications to enterprise security.understanding the people who use these technologies, the environments they work within and the challenges they face is fundamental to building products that are useful, trustworthy and effective.the futures insights team is motorola solutions’ research-led futures and strategic foresight pod, embedded within the broader ux research organization. our team is primarily split across the united states and challenge existing assumptions and investigate opportunities that do not yet fit neatly within today’s organizational boundaries.we approach futuring/futures as a space that is explored and co-created rather than predicted. we seek direction in uncertainty, contradiction, edge cases and emerging behaviours – as well as in established customer needs. the aim is ultimately to create strategic option value for motorola solutions: making uncertain futures more intelligible and identifying high-leverage opportunities earlier.job descriptionas a senior futures design strategist, you’ll help shape horizon 3 (5–10+ year) product opportunities and make sure they lead somewhere. this role is for someone who can dream and be pragmatic. you’ll make futures tangible through artifacts, interfaces and narratives that let users and leaders step inside them. then you’ll make them actionable by turning them into value propositions, opportunity briefs and investment choices the business can act on. as the team’s main design-focused individual contributor, you’ll own the bridge between our futures work and the teams who explore and build. that means making sure every promising concept has a credible next step and a clear owner. you might call yourself a design strategist, innovation strategist, speculative designer or innovation consultant. whatever the title, we want to hear from you if you’ve influence & delivery: present visually compelling strategic options, trade-offs, and risks to c-suite and senior leaders, bringing a clear point of view on which futures to invest in, monitor, or set aside.foresight research & synthesis: partner with researchers to ground concepts in human needs and in market and technology context. contribute to ai-assisted signal scanning and facilitate foresight methods (steep, cla, delphi) to turn weak signals into design hypotheses.practice multiplier: mentor peers, raise the quality of our experiential design, and help show how futures work creates strategic option value across the company.qualificationsexperience: 5+ years in design strategy, innovation strategy, speculative design, strategic foresight, or innovation descriptionwest basin municipal water district (west basin) is a global leader in the water industry in water recycling, conservation, water resource management, and youth and adult education. west basin provides drinking water and recycled water to six cities, four private water utilities, one county waterworks district and one groundwater agency. the district serves a population of nearly one million residents in 17 cities and unincorporated areas along the coastal corridor from palos verdes to malibu. the district is governed by an elected five-member board of directors and is a member detail.desc: director, global enterprise communications - ai, cybersecurity, open source, venturesthe full-spectrum capital one global enterprise communications team is responsible for all aspects of the company’s communications strategy and execution in order to propel business imperatives while promoting and protecting the reputation of capital one. our purview includes corporate and brand media relations, issues and reputation management, financial communications, and associate communications, as well as a full-service content and creative storytelling team that brings the story of capital one to life on internal and external channels. we are communicators, writers, creative directors and multimedia experts, and we are all storytellers. as a central team within global enterprise affairs, we are strategic counselors to our partners throughout the enterprise, sitting at the intersection of value creation and risk mitigation. we help drive business initiatives forward while enhancing the reputation of capital one.we are seeking talented individuals to join our growing communications team. this position requires exceptional judgment, an ability to build relationships in a highly matrixed environment, and a sustained focus on delivering results. creative problem-solving, an ability to read the data and the room, and a passion for storytelling are all critical to success in this role. empathy, teamwork and a sense of humor are essential.about the role:as a director on the corporate communications team, you will lead strategic communications initiatives that enhance capital one’s reputation and support key business objectives in technology and ai. you’ll manage high-impact programs, collaborate with cross-functional teams, and work with internal and external partners to translate technical innovations into compelling narratives and deliver creative and effective communication strategies.this position requires exceptional leadership, judgment, teamwork, results focus, and demonstrated experience in technology communications. an open mind and a passion for finding creative new ways to solve problems and deliver results are essential to the success of this role.primary responsibilities:lead strategic external communications: drive comprehensive external public relations, media relations, and thought leadership campaigns at the intersection of enterprise ai, cyber security, venture capital, and open-source technologies. cross-functional leadership & positioning: partner with business, engineering, science, product, venture capital, and cyber security leadership to translate complex technical innovations into compelling narratives that promote and protect capital one’s reputation in ai, cyber security, venture investments, and open source innovation. executive counsel & media relations: act as a strategic advisor to senior leadership, cultivating and managing relationships with top-tier technology and mainstream media outlets. open source & industry advocacy: partner with the business to advise and help engage with key ai, cyber security, and open-source communities, technology partners, industry consortia, and external stakeholders to promote the company's contributions and leadership in secure, open innovation. serve as a strategic advisor to senior leaders and partners on communications initiatives. lead planning and execution of data-backed, external communications and public relations (pr) campaigns aligned with enterprise and line-of-business priorities. build and maintain relationships with internal and external stakeholders. drive media relations efforts to secure visibility in priority outlets. leverage data to evaluate results, extract insights and optimize future programsoversee team operations, including budgeting, media agencies, and development of best practices. stay informed about industry trends to inform and enhance communication strategies. this role is designated as a hybrid position. you are expected to adhere to capital one's hybrid policy regarding required on-site presence at your designated office location.basic qualifications:bachelor’s degree or military detail.desc: descriptionamazon’s last-mile delivery network touches millions of customers every day — and with that scale comes real scrutiny. legislation, regulatory shifts, and coordinated advocacy campaigns can move fast, and the stories they generate don’t wait for anyone. this role puts you at the center of how amazon identifies, understands, and responds to the issues that matter most to its last-mile delivery operations.as communications manager, last-mile issues and campaigns, you'll own the communications strategy for a portfolio that touches aspects of amazon's last-mile delivery model. last-mile delivery touches regulation, safety, and public trust, and this role sits at the center of how we communicate across all of it. you'll lead strategic narrative development and scenario planning that keeps the team ahead of legislative shifts, emerging campaigns, and related issues. you'll coordinate across relevant business lines and communications teams, partnering with policy comms, field comms, and others, to bring the right expertise to bear at the right moment and ensure amazon speaks with one clear, strategic voice. you'll draft the statements, talking points, and briefing documents that represent amazon externally, and you'll manage the feedback and approval cycles that come with them. you'll spend as much time seeding stories and shaping narratives as you do managing the reactive moments that come with the portfolio.you're a high-judgment communicator who doesn't flinch when things get complicated. you can hold multiple fast-moving situations at once without losing your footing, but what sets you apart is your ability to spot the issue before it breaks and start building the strategy, not just the response. you think clearly under pressure, write precisely on deadline, and know how to bring the right people together at the right moment. you're comfortable as an on-the-record spokesperson, and you know how to work with reporters to shape a story before it spirals. you think like a strategist, connecting dots across policy, operations, and reputation to protect and advance the business. you don't wait to be told there's a problem. you've already mapped the landscape, built the plan, and brought the right people to the table.this is a strong independent contributor role that reports into the core operations communications team within the global operations and workplace reputation team.key job responsibilitiesmanage complex, fast-moving, and unexpected communications challenges with high judgment and professionalism.be precise under tight deadlines and prioritize and manage multiple situations simultaneously.effectively represent amazon as an on-the-record spokesperson.work with reporters to correct and clarify breaking news stories.write, develop, and manage approvals of external communications materials dealing with sensitive and timely topics.participate in multi-stakeholder emergency response meetings to provide insight and guidance from an external communications point-of-view.a day in the lifeyou might start your morning scanning media coverage and legislative trackers to flag any new developments that could affect amazon’s last-mile operations — then pull together a quick brief for a leader heading into a sensitive meeting. by midday, you could be on a call with legal and public policy partners to assess the communications implications of a pending bill or regulatory action, working through the messaging framework and drafting an initial statement. in the afternoon, you may shift to handling a reactive media inquiry on a breaking story, coordinating approvals in real time while staying in close contact with the reporter to manage the narrative. you’ll close out by updating scenario plans for upcoming legislative milestones and checking in with issues managers across the team to make sure nothing’s falling through the cracks.about the teamwe’re a team of strategic communicators responsible for telling the story of how amazon gets people their packages — from the first mile to the last. we work across organizational boundaries to develop integrated communications strategies that inform, engage, and build trust with the audiences that matter most. we use data to shape our decisions, and we anticipate and mitigate reputational headwinds through cross-channel efforts. we value thoughtful collaboration, creative problem-solving, and a commitment to getting the details right.on the issues side of the team, we move fast and we move together. when a legislative campaign or regulatory challenge emerges, we’re the ones coordinating the response — aligning messaging across legal, policy, and business partners and making sure amazon’s voice is clear, consistent, and credible. we’re building for the long term — investing in mechanisms, relationships, and talent that will scale as amazon grows. if you want to do meaningful work alongside colleagues who care deeply about their craft and support each other’s growth, this is the team for you.basic qualifications bachelor's degree 7+ years of recent professional communications or public relations experiencepreferred qualifications experience in verbal and written communication for executive level leaders experience driving direction and alignment with cross-functional teamsamazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.our inclusive culture empowers amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. if you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. if the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your recruiting partner.the base salary range for this position is listed below. your amazon package will include sign-on payments and restricted stock units (rsus). final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. amazon also offers comprehensive benefits including health insurance (medical, dental, vision, prescription, basic life & ad&d insurance and option for supplemental life plans, eap, mental health support, medical advice line, flexible spending accounts, adoption and surrogacy reimbursement coverage), 401(k) matching, paid time off, and parental leave. learn more about our benefits at https://amazon.jobs/en/benefits.usa, ny, new york - 153,500.00 - 207,100.00 usd annuallyusa, tn, nashville - 125,600.00 - 169,500.00 usd annuallyusa, va, chicago, ilapplyfill out our online application.why work with environment illinois? check out 10 reasons: https://environmentillinois.org/why-work-with-us/about environment illinoisenvironment illinois is part of environment america. environment america has one mission: to protect the natural world.we advocate ideas and actions to guide our country onto a greener, healthier path. our story in complex research and translate it into clear, accurate, and engaging content for general audiences. in this role, you will tell stories about chhs-related research, highlighting the with researchers, faculty, university leaders, members of the media, and fellow campus communicators to develop compelling stories, elevating chhs research and initiatives locally, nationally, and internationally.this is a hands-on communications role with plenty of variety. one day, you may be interviewing a researcher, writing about a new study, and pitching the story to national media; another, you may be developing a communications plan for a college initiative, preparing a faculty member for an interview, responding to a media inquiry, or creating multimedia and social media content. the individual in this role will also be responsible for monitoring chhs-related news and online conversations, assessing emerging issues, and recommending messaging and communications strategies.what you'll doresearch storytelling & contentidentify compelling stories across sdsu's research enterprise, particularly in health, science, and human services.translate complex research detail.desc: the quikrete companies is seeking an experienced brand manager - heavy construction materials (hcm) at our corporate office in atlanta, ga. the brand manager is tasked to lead marketing initiatives supporting the company’s heavy construction materials segment, including ready-mix, cement, aggregates (stone, sand, gravel, lightweight aggregates), and asphalt & construction (paving, grading, etc.).reporting to the senior president of the heavy construction materials segment while working closely with the presidents leading the hcm divisions, and the vice president, marketing, quikrete, the brand manager will be responsible for developing and executing marketing initiatives that support sales growth, market share expansion, and brand leadership in the construction materials industry.this role requires both strategic thinking and hands-on execution. while the brand manager will help shape marketing strategy and positioning, approximately 60% of the role is tactical, focused on implementing marketing programs, supporting the sales organization, coordinating campaigns, managing vendors, and developing marketing materials.the position will be supported by a shared services marketing team and cross-functional partners across sales, operations, and leadership to ensure effective execution of marketing initiatives.in addition to marketing responsibilities, the role will support public relations and community engagement efforts, helping maintain strong relationships with industry stakeholders, municipalities, and communities where the company operates.why apply?competitive wages.company provided benefits: medical, dental, vision, company paid life and disability benefits, paid vacation, and 401k.about the roleobjectives of the role:increase market share and sales by driving awareness, trial, and preference for quikrete heavy construction materials products and services.position quikrete as a trusted solutions provider across ready-mix, cement, aggregates, asphalt & construction.support the hcm sales teams by providing marketing programs and tools that help win projects and strengthen customer relationships.monitor competitive activity, market trends, and customer purchasing behavior within the construction materials industry.serve as the product knowledge expert and brand ambassador for the heavy construction materials segment.strengthen industry visibility, public relations, and community engagement in markets where the company operates.primary responsibilities:marketing strategy and brand developmentcontribute to marketing strategies supporting the heavy construction materials segment.help position quikrete as the preferred partner for infrastructure, commercial construction, and large-scale projects.identify opportunities to improve brand visibility, product positioning, market differentiation and brand reputation/community engagement.partner with sales leadership to align marketing initiatives with regional priorities and major project opportunities.tactical marketing execution (significant portion of role)working with the shared services marketing team, lead and execute marketing initiatives including:brand identity and messagingadvertising and campaign executiondigital and social media marketingsales collateral including:project sheetssales presentationssignage and promotional materialscase studies and product literaturetrade shows and industry eventsvendor and agency coordinationmarketing support for product launches and market expansionsthe brand manager will ensure that marketing initiatives are practical, sales-focused, and effectively executed across the business.sales support and market developmentcollaborate closely with sales leadership and regional teams to identify opportunities to support customer acquisition and project wins.develop marketing tools that help the sales organization communicate the value and capabilities of quikrete products and services.support marketing initiatives that strengthen relationships with contractors, developers, infrastructure agencies, and commercial builders.public relations and community engagementmanage public relations initiatives related to the heavy construction materials segment.assist with development of news releases, industry announcements, and thought leadership opportunities.coordinate communications related to major projects, plant investments, and infrastructure initiatives.help strengthen relationships with local communities, municipalities, and industry organizations where company facilities operate.market intelligence and industry awarenessmonitor developments within the cement, aggregates, ready-mix, and infrastructure markets.track competitor activity, pricing dynamics, and market positioning.identify emerging opportunities in infrastructure investment, commercial construction, and regional developmentabout youwe require:strong business acumen and priorities in a fast-paced environment.5-10 years of professional b2b marketing experience, including experience supporting sales organizations.experience across the full marketing mix, including brings new challenges, and we make sure you are prepared for it all. our dedication to continual improvement and hands-on training ensures you are ready for the many new experiences and challenges
